Avasant Generative AI Services 2025 RadarViewTM Survey
Congratulations!  
In recognition of your organization’s position as a key generative AI (Gen AI) services provider, Avasant invites you to provide input for our upcoming RadarView assessment in this space.    
Avasant Generative AI Services 2024 RadarView™ has received great traction from enterprises and providers for insights on the generative AI (Gen AI) services capabilities and the provider landscape. This survey will support data collection for the annual refresh of the 2025 report.
RadarView is a pioneering analytical assessment in key digital technology domains that leverages Avasant’s proprietary Digital Maturity Framework to evaluate leading service providers based on company disclosures and market checks. These assessments will be released to help global organizations identify, assess, and down-select leading service providers to support their digital transformation initiatives. Service providers can also leverage and license these assessments to enhance their public credentials and promote their capabilities to potential clients.
   
You can find more details on the RadarView program here.
   
We invite you to use the online survey to provide input about your Gen AI services to our industry analysts. The survey responses will augment the assessment by Avasant using publicly available information and independent market checks.
ABOUT THE SURVEY
The Generative AI Services 2025 RadarView Survey comprises 21 questions covering the following aspects:
Practice overview and capabilities
Client and project details

Clients are increasingly introducing contractual clauses to mitigate Gen AI risks related to data privacy, governance, and accountability. These include:
Content Accountability: Mandating factuality validation, prompt engineering reviews, red teaming, and model testing to reduce hallucinations and bias in AI-generated content.
Privacy & IP Compliance: Clauses require strict handling of user data during tagging, annotation, and transcription, along with copyright/IP checks and privacy violation reviews.
Human-in-the-Loop Governance: Ensuring human oversight for content moderation, policy enforcement, sentiment analysis, and sensitive data processing.
Model Governance & Explainability: Stipulations for continuous benchmarking, validation, side-by-side evaluations, and model monitoring for transparency and fairness.
Platform Integrity & Safety: Requirements for AI-supported user authentication, identity theft prevention, and platform safety through moderation and community management.
Regulatory Compliance: Legal clauses for jurisdiction-based policy design, regulatory response handling, and legal removal processes.
Audit & Monitoring: Requiring audit logs, model performance tracking, and periodic reviews to ensure responsible AI use.
Scope Control: Limiting AI deployment to approved use cases with clear usage boundaries and content restrictions.
These align with Firstsource’s Trust & Safety and Gen AI services, enabling clients to meet evolving governance and compliance standards effectively.

expected_output: The survey closes on **August 25, 2025, at 5 p.m. Pacific Time**. After that, it becomes inactive and no updates can be made.
context:
Avasant Intelligent Automation Services 2025–2026 RadarViewTM —Survey
Congratulations!
In recognition of your organization’s position as a key intelligent automation services provider, Avasant invites you to provide inputs for our upcoming RadarView assessment in this space.
Intelligent Automation Services 2018 RadarView™, Intelligent Automation Services 2019–2020 RadarView™, Intelligent Automation Services 2020–2021 RadarView™, Intelligent Automation Services 2022–2023 RadarView​™, Intelligent Automation Services 2023–2024 RadarView™, and Intelligent Automation Services 2024–2025 RadarView™ have received great traction from enterprises and providers for insights on the intelligent automation services market and the provider landscape. This survey will support data collection for the annual refresh of the 2025–2026 report.

RadarView is a pioneering analytical assessment in key digital technology domains that leverages Avasant’s proprietary Digital Maturity Framework to evaluate leading service providers based on company disclosures and market checks. These assessments will be released to help global organizations identify, assess, and select leading service providers in nascent technology areas. Service providers can also license these assessments to enhance their public credentials and promote their capabilities to potential clients.

We invite you to use the online survey below to provide input about your intelligent automation practice and capabilities to our industry analysts. The survey responses will augment our assessment using publicly available information and independent market checks.
About the survey
The Intelligent Automation Services 2025–2026 RadarView Survey comprises 25 questions across four key sections:
Offerings and capabilities
Client and project details
Practice details
Strategy and investment plans
Instructions    
​Please complete the survey and submit your responses before August 25, 2025, at 5 p.m. Pacific Time. After that, the survey will become inactive, and no modification or update will be possible.
The survey allows for stop-start completion through an automatic save feature. There is no separate “Save” button.
There are prescribed word limits for descriptive questions, and we recommend brief and self-explanatory responses.
Avasant does not guarantee that the submission of this survey automatically qualifies or disqualifies any service provider from the subsequent stages of the RadarView assessment.
For any clarifications on the survey, please reach out to radarview@avasant.com.

As part of the input collection, we suggest you schedule a briefing with your intelligent automation leaders and our analysts. To schedule the briefing, please email saurav.jayant@avasant.com with the subject line “Briefing schedule request — Intelligent Automation Services.”
Please provide the following details of the organization representative submitting the response:
Organization name __________________ Firstsource Solutions ______________________________
Respondent name __________________Pooja Heda______________________________
Title ______________________Director, Marketing__________________________
Email _________________________ Pooja.Heda@firstsource.com _______________________
Phone number ________________________________________________
Defining intelligent automation
For this survey, Avasant defines intelligent automation (IA) as an application of robotic process automation (RPA), machine learning (ML), natural language processing (NLP), artificial intelligence (AI), or other third-party or in-house predictive technologies and tools, either in cohesion or disparately, to automate IT, enterprise, and industry-specific processes based on business semantics, historical data, and contextual understanding.
Typical examples include automating user actions in an invoice reconciliation process, implementing chatbot capabilities to enhance a banking customer’s self-service capabilities, automatic categorization of IT help desk tickets through ML, predictive network maintenance, or orchestration of automation across various enterprise processes. Please keep this definition in mind when responding to this survey.
Offerings and capabilities
Please provide details of your key intelligent automation service offerings with a brief description.
Refer to these descriptions when selecting the options for respective offerings.
Advisory and consulting: This refers to assessing the organization’s goals and evaluating intelligent automation’s applicability and impact on the business, helping identify and prioritize use cases for transformation.
Proof of concept (POC) development: This refers to helping design and implement POCs and defining anticipated value for the identified use cases.
Build and test: This refers to implementing an intelligent automation solution on the selected platform for the necessary scale, performance, and security.
Integration services: This refers to assessing legacy systems and helping introduce intelligent automation into enterprise IT architecture.
Development and maintenance: This refers to enabling the deployment of intelligent automation solutions across the network and ensuring changes and updates.
Please provide details of the reusable assets, tools, and frameworks that your organization has created for delivering intelligent automation services. Do not include client POC assets. Limit the description of each asset to under 500 characters.

Avasant Intelligent Automation Services 2025–2026 RadarViewTM —Survey
Congratulations!
In recognition of your organization’s position as a key intelligent automation services provider, Avasant invites you to provide inputs for our upcoming RadarView assessment in this space.
Intelligent Automation Services 2018 RadarView™, Intelligent Automation Services 2019–2020 RadarView™, Intelligent Automation Services 2020–2021 RadarView™, Intelligent Automation Services 2022–2023 RadarView​™, Intelligent Automation Services 2023–2024 RadarView™, and Intelligent Automation Services 2024–2025 RadarView™ have received great traction from enterprises and providers for insights on the intelligent automation services market and the provider landscape. This survey will support data collection for the annual refresh of the 2025–2026 report.

RadarView is a pioneering analytical assessment in key digital technology domains that leverages Avasant’s proprietary Digital Maturity Framework to evaluate leading service providers based on company disclosures and market checks. These assessments will be released to help global organizations identify, assess, and select leading service providers in nascent technology areas. Service providers can also license these assessments to enhance their public credentials and promote their capabilities to potential clients.

We invite you to use the online survey below to provide input about your intelligent automation practice and capabilities to our industry analysts. The survey responses will augment our assessment using publicly available information and independent market checks.
About the survey
The Intelligent Automation Services 2025–2026 RadarView Survey comprises 25 questions across four key sections:
Offerings and capabilities
Client and project details
Practice details
Strategy and investment plans
Instructions    
​Please complete the survey and submit your responses before August 25, 2025, at 5 p.m. Pacific Time. After that, the survey will become inactive, and no modification or update will be possible.
The survey allows for stop-start completion through an automatic save feature. There is no separate “Save” button.
There are prescribed word limits for descriptive questions, and we recommend brief and self-explanatory responses.
Avasant does not guarantee that the submission of this survey automatically qualifies or disqualifies any service provider from the subsequent stages of the RadarView assessment.
For any clarifications on the survey, please reach out to radarview@avasant.com.

As part of the input collection, we suggest you schedule a briefing with your intelligent automation leaders and our analysts. To schedule the briefing, please email saurav.jayant@avasant.com with the subject line “Briefing schedule request — Intelligent Automation Services.”
Please provide the following details of the organization representative submitting the response:
Organization name __________________ Firstsource Solutions ______________________________
Respondent name __________________Pooja Heda______________________________
Title ______________________Director, Marketing__________________________
Email _________________________ Pooja.Heda@firstsource.com _______________________
Phone number ________________________________________________
Defining intelligent automation
For this survey, Avasant defines intelligent automation (IA) as an application of robotic process automation (RPA), machine learning (ML), natural language processing (NLP), artificial intelligence (AI), or other third-party or in-house predictive technologies and tools, either in cohesion or disparately, to automate IT, enterprise, and industry-specific processes based on business semantics, historical data, and contextual understanding.
Typical examples include automating user actions in an invoice reconciliation process, implementing chatbot capabilities to enhance a banking customer’s self-service capabilities, automatic categorization of IT help desk tickets through ML, predictive network maintenance, or orchestration of automation across various enterprise processes. Please keep this definition in mind when responding to this survey.
Offerings and capabilities
Please provide details of your key intelligent automation service offerings with a brief description.
Refer to these descriptions when selecting the options for respective offerings.
Advisory and consulting: This refers to assessing the organization’s goals and evaluating intelligent automation’s applicability and impact on the business, helping identify and prioritize use cases for transformation.
Proof of concept (POC) development: This refers to helping design and implement POCs and defining anticipated value for the identified use cases.
Build and test: This refers to implementing an intelligent automation solution on the selected platform for the necessary scale, performance, and security.
Integration services: This refers to assessing legacy systems and helping introduce intelligent automation into enterprise IT architecture.
Development and maintenance: This refers to enabling the deployment of intelligent automation solutions across the network and ensuring changes and updates.
Please provide details of the reusable assets, tools, and frameworks that your organization has created for delivering intelligent automation services. Do not include client POC assets. Limit the description of each asset to under 500 characters.
Response: 
We organize our reusable assets, tools, and frameworks into six broad categories:
Intelligent Document Processing (IDP)
Process Mining
Conversational AI
Automation Workflows
Next-GenAI Solutions
Agentic Workflow
Depending on the use case, we can leverage one or seamlessly weave together multiple categories to deliver integrated, high-impact automation solutions.
Please list the most complex use cases where you have utilized AI agents to automate business processes in an enterprise environment. Describe how these automations were implemented. 
Are you developing multiagent frameworks that utilize multiple AI agents to enhance system autonomy and handle diverse, complex queries for business process automation? 
(Please limit the description to 1,000 characters.)
If you are implementing a multiagent approach, please provide the ratio of multiagent approach implementations to platform-based approach implementations.
(The total should sum up to 100%.)
The first use case highlighted in Q3 — Healthcare Claims Adjudication & Correspondence Automation — is designed on a multi-agent framework.
The other two use cases — Transforming Student Support with Agentic AI for a Global Education & Talent Provider and Mortgage Underwriting – Income Validation Agent — also follow an open multi-agent approach leveraging frameworks such as LangChain and LangGraph.
In parallel, we are evaluating independent platforms like Lyzr, Microsoft AI Foundry, and Applied AI to industrialize our platform-based strategy. A steady pipeline of workflows and industry solutions is being built to adopt this model, ensuring balance between flexibility of multi-agent frameworks and governance, scalability, and standardization offered by platforms.
Please provide the total number of automation CoEs established/initiated for enterprises as of June 30, 2024, and June 30, 2025.
What are the top three challenges encountered when establishing these automation CoEs, and how are you addressing them? Please provide detailed descriptions.
Please provide the percentage split of your organization’s intelligent automation implementations based on the following two categories.
Definitions
Standalone automation implementations: These include automation platform or bot deployments.
Automation as a part of broader digital transformation contracts: This includes automation that involves integration with other technologies such as blockchain, IoT, and cybersecurity; for example, automation of security policy creation and configuration, automated asset tracking
and records management on the blockchain platform, and automated IoT data collection from wearables.
Please provide the details of innovation labs supporting intelligent automation services.
Please provide the head count of overall intelligent automation services professionals and the number of delivery support centers for intelligent automation services.
Client and project details
Please provide the percentage split of your intelligent automation services clients in the following three categories:
IT automation: This includes processes such as IT operations monitoring and service desk.
Enterprise automation: This includes processes such as finance and accounting, human resources, customer service, and procurement.
Industry-specific automation: This includes processes such as healthcare claims processing, card activation, bill of material generation, and ticketing.
Please provide the total number of intelligent automation services clients across different industry verticals.
Please provide the percentage split of your client base across the enterprise automation maturity phases.
Definitions
Robotic process automation (RPA): This refers to rule-based automation for back- and front-office systems.
End-to-end business process automation: This refers to automating entire end-to-end processes (procure-to-pay and order-to-cash, among others) with a human in the loop. 
Hyperautomation: This covers a range of solutions across the automation value chain, including AI, RPA, integration platform as a service (iPaaS), intelligent business process management (iBPM), and intelligent document processing (IDP), to enable autonomous business decision-making. 
Industrialization: This refers to building intelligent automation CoEs.
Please share the key case studies from the past 12 months that demonstrate the differentiating capabilities of your intelligent automation services. Feel free to provide use cases for more complex automation involving semantic and predictive automation.
Please limit the description of each case study to under 500 characters.
Response:
We have mapped our six broad categories of reusable assets and tools (outlined in Q.2) to the relevant use cases. This illustrates the clear linkage between our offerings, these assets/tools, and their application in delivering Intelligent Automation services. 
What are the various commercial models you offer your clients?

Practice details

Please provide percentages that add up to 100%.
Please provide the number of certified intelligent automation employees in your organization and the certification goal for the next 12 months.

For example, you can mention external certifications such as RPA Developer Foundation (UiPath), MuleSoft Certified Developer, and RPA partner certifications from UiPath, SS&C Blue Prism, Automation Anywhere, and others.
Please provide a unique number for each category. The total for each category should not exceed the total employee strength in the current year.
Please provide the names of your top 10 partners and the value they add to your intelligent automation practices.
Strategy and investment plans
Please describe your organization’s intelligent automation services plan for the next 12 months.
You may cover topics such as practice vision and road map, new service offerings, partnership strategy, head count, and revenue goals.
​Please provide a brief response, preferably in bullet points, under 1,500 characters.
Please indicate the budget for planned investments in the intelligent automation services space over the next 12 months (in USD million).
Please list all the prototype solutions related to intelligent automation services to be commercialized over the next 12 months.
Please limit the description of each solution to under 500 characters.
Please describe the distribution of the planned investment among different activities.
Please provide indicative percentages that add up to 100%​.
Please provide details of any intelligent automation services-related acquisitions your organization has made in the past 12 months.
Additional information
We strongly recommend uploading additional documents related to your intelligent automation services capabilities and strategy.    
Please note that you can upload a single file of up to 100MB. If you wish to share multiple files, please zip them into one file to upload.

Avasant Intelligent Automation Services 2025–2026 RadarViewTM —Survey
Congratulations!
In recognition of your organization’s position as a key intelligent automation services provider, Avasant invites you to provide inputs for our upcoming RadarView assessment in this space.
Intelligent Automation Services 2018 RadarView™, Intelligent Automation Services 2019–2020 RadarView™, Intelligent Automation Services 2020–2021 RadarView™, Intelligent Automation Services 2022–2023 RadarView​™, Intelligent Automation Services 2023–2024 RadarView™, and Intelligent Automation Services 2024–2025 RadarView™ have received great traction from enterprises and providers for insights on the intelligent automation services market and the provider landscape. This survey will support data collection for the annual refresh of the 2025–2026 report.

RadarView is a pioneering analytical assessment in key digital technology domains that leverages Avasant’s proprietary Digital Maturity Framework to evaluate leading service providers based on company disclosures and market checks. These assessments will be released to help global organizations identify, assess, and select leading service providers in nascent technology areas. Service providers can also license these assessments to enhance their public credentials and promote their capabilities to potential clients.

We invite you to use the online survey below to provide input about your intelligent automation practice and capabilities to our industry analysts. The survey responses will augment our assessment using publicly available information and independent market checks.
About the survey
The Intelligent Automation Services 2025–2026 RadarView Survey comprises 25 questions across four key sections:
Offerings and capabilities
Client and project details
Practice details
Strategy and investment plans
Instructions    
​Please complete the survey and submit your responses before August 25, 2025, at 5 p.m. Pacific Time. After that, the survey will become inactive, and no modification or update will be possible.
The survey allows for stop-start completion through an automatic save feature. There is no separate “Save” button.
There are prescribed word limits for descriptive questions, and we recommend brief and self-explanatory responses.
Avasant does not guarantee that the submission of this survey automatically qualifies or disqualifies any service provider from the subsequent stages of the RadarView assessment.
For any clarifications on the survey, please reach out to radarview@avasant.com.

As part of the input collection, we suggest you schedule a briefing with your intelligent automation leaders and our analysts. To schedule the briefing, please email saurav.jayant@avasant.com with the subject line “Briefing schedule request — Intelligent Automation Services.”
Please provide the following details of the organization representative submitting the response:
Organization name __________________ Firstsource Solutions ______________________________
Respondent name __________________Pooja Heda______________________________
Title ______________________Director, Marketing__________________________
Email _________________________ Pooja.Heda@firstsource.com _______________________
Phone number ________________________________________________
Defining intelligent automation
For this survey, Avasant defines intelligent automation (IA) as an application of robotic process automation (RPA), machine learning (ML), natural language processing (NLP), artificial intelligence (AI), or other third-party or in-house predictive technologies and tools, either in cohesion or disparately, to automate IT, enterprise, and industry-specific processes based on business semantics, historical data, and contextual understanding.
Typical examples include automating user actions in an invoice reconciliation process, implementing chatbot capabilities to enhance a banking customer’s self-service capabilities, automatic categorization of IT help desk tickets through ML, predictive network maintenance, or orchestration of automation across various enterprise processes. Please keep this definition in mind when responding to this survey.
Offerings and capabilities
Please provide details of your key intelligent automation service offerings with a brief description.
Refer to these descriptions when selecting the options for respective offerings.
Advisory and consulting: This refers to assessing the organization’s goals and evaluating intelligent automation’s applicability and impact on the business, helping identify and prioritize use cases for transformation.
Proof of concept (POC) development: This refers to helping design and implement POCs and defining anticipated value for the identified use cases.
Build and test: This refers to implementing an intelligent automation solution on the selected platform for the necessary scale, performance, and security.
Integration services: This refers to assessing legacy systems and helping introduce intelligent automation into enterprise IT architecture.
Development and maintenance: This refers to enabling the deployment of intelligent automation solutions across the network and ensuring changes and updates.
Please provide details of the reusable assets, tools, and frameworks that your organization has created for delivering intelligent automation services. Do not include client POC assets. Limit the description of each asset to under 500 characters.

Are you developing multiagent frameworks that utilize multiple AI agents to enhance system autonomy and handle diverse, complex queries for business process automation? 
(Please limit the description to 1,000 characters.)
If you are implementing a multiagent approach, please provide the ratio of multiagent approach implementations to platform-based approach implementations.

The first use case highlighted in Q3 — Healthcare Claims Adjudication & Correspondence Automation — is designed on a multi-agent framework.

In parallel, we are evaluating independent platforms like Lyzr, Microsoft AI Foundry, and Applied AI to industrialize our platform-based strategy. A steady pipeline of workflows and industry solutions is being built to adopt this model, ensuring balance between flexibility of multi-agent frameworks and governance, scalability, and standardization offered by platforms.

Industry-specific automation: This includes processes such as healthcare claims processing, card activation, bill of material generation, and ticketing.
Please provide the total number of intelligent automation services clients across different industry verticals.
Please provide the percentage split of your client base across the enterprise automation maturity phases.
Definitions
Robotic process automation (RPA): This refers to rule-based automation for back- and front-office systems.
End-to-end business process automation: This refers to automating entire end-to-end processes (procure-to-pay and order-to-cash, among others) with a human in the loop. 
Hyperautomation: This covers a range of solutions across the automation value chain, including AI, RPA, integration platform as a service (iPaaS), intelligent business process management (iBPM), and intelligent document processing (IDP), to enable autonomous business decision-making. 
Industrialization: This refers to building intelligent automation CoEs.
Please share the key case studies from the past 12 months that demonstrate the differentiating capabilities of your intelligent automation services. Feel free to provide use cases for more complex automation involving semantic and predictive automation.
Please limit the description of each case study to under 500 characters.

Please provide the names of your top 10 partners and the value they add to your intelligent automation practices.
Strategy and investment plans
Please describe your organization’s intelligent automation services plan for the next 12 months.
You may cover topics such as practice vision and road map, new service offerings, partnership strategy, head count, and revenue goals.
​Please provide a brief response, preferably in bullet points, under 1,500 characters.
Please indicate the budget for planned investments in the intelligent automation services space over the next 12 months (in USD million).
Please list all the prototype solutions related to intelligent automation services to be commercialized over the next 12 months.
Please limit the description of each solution to under 500 characters.

Please provide details of any intelligent automation services-related acquisitions your organization has made in the past 12 months.
Additional information
We strongly recommend uploading additional documents related to your intelligent automation services capabilities and strategy.    
Please note that you can upload a single file of up to 100MB. If you wish to share multiple files, please zip them into one file to upload.

input: If a provider seeks Avasant’s 2026 RadarView inclusion, what applied AI practice inputs must it submit?
expected_output:
To be considered for Avasant’s Applied AI Services 2026 RadarView, the provider must submit the online survey with details on its applied AI practice and capabilities. The survey covers 31 questions across six sections, including:

- Practice overview and capabilities
- Client and project details
- Human capital overview
- Industry ecosystem overview
- Strategy and investment plans
- Organization representative details

Avasant asks providers to share inputs such as AI offerings, reusable solutions/accelerators, Responsible AI capabilities, client engagements, revenue, talent, partnerships, investments, and supporting documents. The submission deadline is July 20, 2026, 5 p.m. Pacific Time.
context:
Avasant Applied AI Services 2026 RadarView™ Survey
Congratulations!  
In recognition of your organization’s position as a key AI and automation services provider, Avasant invites you to provide inputs for our upcoming Applied AI Services 2026 RadarView assessment.

Applied AI Services 2024 RadarView and Applied AI Services 2025 RadarView have received great traction from enterprises and providers for their insights about the applied AI market and the provider landscape they contain. This survey will support data collection for the annual refresh of the 2026 report.

RadarView is a pioneering analytical assessment in key digital technology domains that leverages Avasant’s proprietary Digital Maturity Framework to evaluate leading service providers based on company disclosures and market checks. These assessments will be released to help global organizations identify, assess, and down-select leading service providers in nascent technology areas. Service providers can also license these assessments to enhance their public credentials and promote their capabilities to potential clients.
​
​You can find more details on RadarView here.
We invite you to use the online survey below to provide input about you Applied AI practice and capabilities to our industry analysts. The survey responses will augment the assessment by Avasant using publicly available information and market checks.
About the survey
The Applied AI RadarView Survey comprises 31 questions across six key sections:   	
Practice overview and capabilities
Client and project details
Human capital overview
Industry ecosystem overview
Strategy and investment plans 
Instructions    
​Please complete the survey and submit your responses before July 20, 2026, 5 p.m. Pacific Time.
The survey will become inactive after that, and no modification or update will be possible.
The survey allows for stop-start completion through an automatic save feature. There is no separate “Save” button.
There are prescribed word limits in descriptive questions, and we recommend brief and self-explanatory responses. ​Avasant does not guarantee that the submission of this survey automatically qualifies or disqualifies any service provider from the subsequent stages of the RadarView assessment.
For any clarifications on the survey, please reach out to abhisekh.satapathy@avasant.com.
As part of the input collection, we suggest that you schedule a briefing from your applied AI leaders with our analysts. For scheduling, please send an email with the subject “Briefing schedule request.”

The capabilities and offerings considered in this survey are:
​Applied AI strategy and transformation services (enterprise-wide AI strategy, including road map definition, operating model and CoE design, use-case identification and prioritization, AI readiness assessment, responsible AI advisory, foundation model selection and build-vs.-buy advisory, talent strategy, and value realization frameworks)
AI engineering and implementation services (industry- and domain-specific AI solution design, foundation model customization through fine-tuning, prompt engineering, and domain adaptation, AI orchestration platform design and deployment, agentic AI workflow implementation, pre-production evaluation and adversarial testing, and production deployment)
AI managed services and operations (AI model life cycle management, including drift monitoring and retraining, AI application life cycle management, continuous output quality monitoring, including hallucination detection and SLA management, AI FinOps covering token usage, compute cost optimization, and ROI tracking, ongoing risk, compliance, and bias monitoring, and change management and exception handling)
Please provide details of reusable AI solutions and accelerators created by your organization. Do not repeat services listed in the previous question . Focus only on packaged, reusable solutions, platforms, accelerators, and IP deployed across multiple client engagements.
Categories:
AI development and deployment accelerators (fine-tuning toolkits, prompt libraries, RAG templates, model evaluation harnesses, CI/CD pipelines for AI, and production deployment frameworks)
AI operations and monitoring platforms (MLOps, LLMOps, and AgentOps pipelines, drift detection engines, performance dashboards, SLA tracking, AI FinOps tools covering token usage and compute cost optimization)
AI governance and responsible AI tools (bias detection tools, explainability modules, guardrail engines, compliance templates, audit trail generators, and policy enforcement frameworks)
Data and knowledge engineering tools (data pipelines, vector database connectors, knowledge graph builders, synthetic data generators, feature stores, and data quality validation tools)
Industry, domain, and use-case solution accelerators (prebuilt vertical solutions, domain-specific function solutions, and modular use-case components such as document extraction, summarization, and entity recognition)
Prebuilt orchestration and workflow blueprints (multi-agent coordination patterns, agentic workflow templates, event-driven orchestration configurations, tool-use and API chaining blueprints, and end-to-end process automation reference architectures)
Please indicate the AI services and solutions your organization offers, along with a brief description of their scope and delivery model.

Definition:											     
AI infrastructure management services: Design, deployment, and managed operations of infrastructure purpose-built for AI workloads, including GPU and accelerator orchestration, model serving and inference optimization, runtime scaling, and cost-performance management.
AI training services: Structured, role-based enablement programs for enterprise teams covering AI development, agent supervision, operational adoption, and AI governance readiness, delivered beyond one-time awareness or introductory training sessions.
Sovereign AI services: Design, deployment, and managed operation of AI workloads within jurisdiction-bound, client-controlled environments, including sovereign compute and infrastructure setup, regional data residency enforcement, region-specific model training or fine-tuning, and in-country delivery supported by local delivery teams and accredited regional partners, in line with national AI regulations.
Training data generation services: Services for generating, augmenting, and validating training and test data for AI systems, including synthetic data creation, simulation environments, data quality validation, and human feedback pipelines used for model training, tuning, and evaluation.
Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) services: Structured short-term (4–6 week) embedded engagements to design AI agent architectures and orchestration workflows, covering system blueprints, integration with enterprise data and applications, and governance model alignment.
AI assurance and red-teaming services: Structured engagements to validate AI models and agentic systems for performance, safety, and compliance, including adversarial testing (prompt injection, hallucination, data leakage), bias evaluation, and governance validation.
Please indicate which Responsible AI (RAI) capabilities your organization provides. Focus on capabilities related to AI governance, risk management, compliance, security, and trust, and avoid repeating generic AI services listed above
Definition:
Standalone RAI strategy and advisory services: Advisory services focused on AI risk assessment, use-case classification, and regulatory and governance alignment across predictive AI, Gen AI, and agentic systems
RAI guardrails, policy enforcement, and governance frameworks: Proprietary solutions and frameworks that enforce policies, safety controls, and governance rules across AI model behavior, Gen AI outputs, and agent actions

Transparency, auditability, and incident management solutions: Capabilities that provide explainability, end-to-end logging, audit trails, and incident response mechanisms, including overrides and rollback for AI systems

Defining applied AI services

Applied AI services comprise consulting, engineering, implementation, integration, and managed services that help enterprises embed AI capabilities into applications, workflows, and business processes. The scope includes the application of deterministic AI, generative AI, and agentic AI capabilities across enterprise environments to improve operational efficiency, enhance customer experiences, and enable new revenue opportunities. It also includes forward-looking AI paradigms, including neuromorphic AI, physical AI, and quantum AI.

Scope of coverage

Strategy and advisory
- AI readiness assessment across data, infrastructure, talent, and governance maturity
- Use case identification, prioritization, and quantified value case development
- Foundation model selection and build vs. buy architecture advisory
- Responsible AI framework design covering ethics, bias, and regulatory compliance
- AI CoE design and scaling operating model
- AI talent strategy, workforce skilling, and internal capability building
- Early pilot testing in new-age AI paradigms

AI engineering and implementation
- Industry- and domain-specific AI solution design, customization, and production deployment
- Foundation model customization through fine-tuning, domain adaptation, and prompt engineering
- RAG architecture design and enterprise knowledge base engineering
- Pre-production evaluation framework design, red teaming, and adversarial robustness testing
- AI orchestration platform design and deployment

Managed services and operations
- AI model life cycle management, including drift monitoring and retraining
- LLMOps and inference optimization covering latency, cost, and throughput
- Continuous output quality monitoring, including hallucination detection and SLA management
- Ongoing AI risk, regulatory compliance, and bias monitoring with audit support
- Change management and exception handling support
- AI FinOps/Tokenomics covering token usage, compute cost optimization, and ROI tracking

context:
Avasant Applied AI Services 2026 RadarView™ Survey
Congratulations!  
In recognition of your organization’s position as a key AI and automation services provider, Avasant invites you to provide inputs for our upcoming Applied AI Services 2026 RadarView assessment.

Applied AI Services 2024 RadarView and Applied AI Services 2025 RadarView have received great traction from enterprises and providers for their insights about the applied AI market and the provider landscape they contain. This survey will support data collection for the annual refresh of the 2026 report.

RadarView is a pioneering analytical assessment in key digital technology domains that leverages Avasant’s proprietary Digital Maturity Framework to evaluate leading service providers based on company disclosures and market checks. These assessments will be released to help global organizations identify, assess, and down-select leading service providers in nascent technology areas. Service providers can also license these assessments to enhance their public credentials and promote their capabilities to potential clients.
​
​You can find more details on RadarView here.
We invite you to use the online survey below to provide input about you Applied AI practice and capabilities to our industry analysts. The survey responses will augment the assessment by Avasant using publicly available information and market checks.
About the survey
The Applied AI RadarView Survey comprises 31 questions across six key sections:   	
Practice overview and capabilities
Client and project details
Human capital overview
Industry ecosystem overview
Strategy and investment plans 
Instructions    
​Please complete the survey and submit your responses before July 20, 2026, 5 p.m. Pacific Time.
The survey will become inactive after that, and no modification or update will be possible.
The survey allows for stop-start completion through an automatic save feature. There is no separate “Save” button.
There are prescribed word limits in descriptive questions, and we recommend brief and self-explanatory responses. ​Avasant does not guarantee that the submission of this survey automatically qualifies or disqualifies any service provider from the subsequent stages of the RadarView assessment.
For any clarifications on the survey, please reach out to abhisekh.satapathy@avasant.com.
As part of the input collection, we suggest that you schedule a briefing from your applied AI leaders with our analysts. For scheduling, please send an email with the subject “Briefing schedule request.”

Practice overview and capabilities

Limit the description of each offering to under 500 characters.
The capabilities and offerings considered in this survey are:
​Applied AI strategy and transformation services (enterprise-wide AI strategy, including road map definition, operating model and CoE design, use-case identification and prioritization, AI readiness assessment, responsible AI advisory, foundation model selection and build-vs.-buy advisory, talent strategy, and value realization frameworks)
AI engineering and implementation services (industry- and domain-specific AI solution design, foundation model customization through fine-tuning, prompt engineering, and domain adaptation, AI orchestration platform design and deployment, agentic AI workflow implementation, pre-production evaluation and adversarial testing, and production deployment)
AI managed services and operations (AI model life cycle management, including drift monitoring and retraining, AI application life cycle management, continuous output quality monitoring, including hallucination detection and SLA management, AI FinOps covering token usage, compute cost optimization, and ROI tracking, ongoing risk, compliance, and bias monitoring, and change management and exception handling)

Categories:

AI operations and monitoring platforms (MLOps, LLMOps, and AgentOps pipelines, drift detection engines, performance dashboards, SLA tracking, AI FinOps tools covering token usage and compute cost optimization)
AI governance and responsible AI tools (bias detection tools, explainability modules, guardrail engines, compliance templates, audit trail generators, and policy enforcement frameworks)
Data and knowledge engineering tools (data pipelines, vector database connectors, knowledge graph builders, synthetic data generators, feature stores, and data quality validation tools)
Industry, domain, and use-case solution accelerators (prebuilt vertical solutions, domain-specific function solutions, and modular use-case components such as document extraction, summarization, and entity recognition)
Prebuilt orchestration and workflow blueprints (multi-agent coordination patterns, agentic workflow templates, event-driven orchestration configurations, tool-use and API chaining blueprints, and end-to-end process automation reference architectures)
Please indicate the AI services and solutions your organization offers, along with a brief description of their scope and delivery model.

Definition:											     
AI infrastructure management services: Design, deployment, and managed operations of infrastructure purpose-built for AI workloads, including GPU and accelerator orchestration, model serving and inference optimization, runtime scaling, and cost-performance management.
AI training services: Structured, role-based enablement programs for enterprise teams covering AI development, agent supervision, operational adoption, and AI governance readiness, delivered beyond one-time awareness or introductory training sessions.
Sovereign AI services: Design, deployment, and managed operation of AI workloads within jurisdiction-bound, client-controlled environments, including sovereign compute and infrastructure setup, regional data residency enforcement, region-specific model training or fine-tuning, and in-country delivery supported by local delivery teams and accredited regional partners, in line with national AI regulations.
Training data generation services: Services for generating, augmenting, and validating training and test data for AI systems, including synthetic data creation, simulation environments, data quality validation, and human feedback pipelines used for model training, tuning, and evaluation.
Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) services: Structured short-term (4–6 week) embedded engagements to design AI agent architectures and orchestration workflows, covering system blueprints, integration with enterprise data and applications, and governance model alignment.
AI assurance and red-teaming services: Structured engagements to validate AI models and agentic systems for performance, safety, and compliance, including adversarial testing (prompt injection, hallucination, data leakage), bias evaluation, and governance validation.
Please indicate which Responsible AI (RAI) capabilities your organization provides. Focus on capabilities related to AI governance, risk management, compliance, security, and trust, and avoid repeating generic AI services listed above

RAI guardrails, policy enforcement, and governance frameworks: Proprietary solutions and frameworks that enforce policies, safety controls, and governance rules across AI model behavior, Gen AI outputs, and agent actions

Transparency, auditability, and incident management solutions: Capabilities that provide explainability, end-to-end logging, audit trails, and incident response mechanisms, including overrides and rollback for AI systems
Data protection and privacy controls: Controls and services for protecting sensitive data across AI pipelines, including Personally Identifiable Information (PII) detection, data isolation, residency enforcement, and access management

Avasant Applied AI Services 2026 RadarView™ Survey
Congratulations!  
In recognition of your organization’s position as a key AI and automation services provider, Avasant invites you to provide inputs for our upcoming Applied AI Services 2026 RadarView assessment.

Applied AI Services 2024 RadarView and Applied AI Services 2025 RadarView have received great traction from enterprises and providers for their insights about the applied AI market and the provider landscape they contain. This survey will support data collection for the annual refresh of the 2026 report.

RadarView is a pioneering analytical assessment in key digital technology domains that leverages Avasant’s proprietary Digital Maturity Framework to evaluate leading service providers based on company disclosures and market checks. These assessments will be released to help global organizations identify, assess, and down-select leading service providers in nascent technology areas. Service providers can also license these assessments to enhance their public credentials and promote their capabilities to potential clients.
​
​You can find more details on RadarView here.
We invite you to use the online survey below to provide input about you Applied AI practice and capabilities to our industry analysts. The survey responses will augment the assessment by Avasant using publicly available information and market checks.
About the survey
The Applied AI RadarView Survey comprises 31 questions across six key sections:   	
Practice overview and capabilities
Client and project details
Human capital overview
Industry ecosystem overview
Strategy and investment plans 
Instructions    
​Please complete the survey and submit your responses before July 20, 2026, 5 p.m. Pacific Time.
The survey will become inactive after that, and no modification or update will be possible.
The survey allows for stop-start completion through an automatic save feature. There is no separate “Save” button.
There are prescribed word limits in descriptive questions, and we recommend brief and self-explanatory responses. ​Avasant does not guarantee that the submission of this survey automatically qualifies or disqualifies any service provider from the subsequent stages of the RadarView assessment.
For any clarifications on the survey, please reach out to abhisekh.satapathy@avasant.com.
As part of the input collection, we suggest that you schedule a briefing from your applied AI leaders with our analysts. For scheduling, please send an email with the subject “Briefing schedule request.”
Please provide the following details of the organization representative submitting the response:
Organization name: ___________
Respondent name: _____________
Title: _____________
Email: ____________
Phone number: ______________
Practice overview and capabilities
Please provide a list of your key applied AI offerings along with a brief description.
Limit the description of each offering to under 500 characters.
The capabilities and offerings considered in this survey are:
​Applied AI strategy and transformation services (enterprise-wide AI strategy, including road map definition, operating model and CoE design, use-case identification and prioritization, AI readiness assessment, responsible AI advisory, foundation model selection and build-vs.-buy advisory, talent strategy, and value realization frameworks)
AI engineering and implementation services (industry- and domain-specific AI solution design, foundation model customization through fine-tuning, prompt engineering, and domain adaptation, AI orchestration platform design and deployment, agentic AI workflow implementation, pre-production evaluation and adversarial testing, and production deployment)
AI managed services and operations (AI model life cycle management, including drift monitoring and retraining, AI application life cycle management, continuous output quality monitoring, including hallucination detection and SLA management, AI FinOps covering token usage, compute cost optimization, and ROI tracking, ongoing risk, compliance, and bias monitoring, and change management and exception handling)
Please provide details of reusable AI solutions and accelerators created by your organization. Do not repeat services listed in the previous question . Focus only on packaged, reusable solutions, platforms, accelerators, and IP deployed across multiple client engagements.
Categories:
AI development and deployment accelerators (fine-tuning toolkits, prompt libraries, RAG templates, model evaluation harnesses, CI/CD pipelines for AI, and production deployment frameworks)
AI operations and monitoring platforms (MLOps, LLMOps, and AgentOps pipelines, drift detection engines, performance dashboards, SLA tracking, AI FinOps tools covering token usage and compute cost optimization)
AI governance and responsible AI tools (bias detection tools, explainability modules, guardrail engines, compliance templates, audit trail generators, and policy enforcement frameworks)
Data and knowledge engineering tools (data pipelines, vector database connectors, knowledge graph builders, synthetic data generators, feature stores, and data quality validation tools)
Industry, domain, and use-case solution accelerators (prebuilt vertical solutions, domain-specific function solutions, and modular use-case components such as document extraction, summarization, and entity recognition)
Prebuilt orchestration and workflow blueprints (multi-agent coordination patterns, agentic workflow templates, event-driven orchestration configurations, tool-use and API chaining blueprints, and end-to-end process automation reference architectures)
Please indicate the AI services and solutions your organization offers, along with a brief description of their scope and delivery model.

Definition:											     
AI infrastructure management services: Design, deployment, and managed operations of infrastructure purpose-built for AI workloads, including GPU and accelerator orchestration, model serving and inference optimization, runtime scaling, and cost-performance management.
AI training services: Structured, role-based enablement programs for enterprise teams covering AI development, agent supervision, operational adoption, and AI governance readiness, delivered beyond one-time awareness or introductory training sessions.
Sovereign AI services: Design, deployment, and managed operation of AI workloads within jurisdiction-bound, client-controlled environments, including sovereign compute and infrastructure setup, regional data residency enforcement, region-specific model training or fine-tuning, and in-country delivery supported by local delivery teams and accredited regional partners, in line with national AI regulations.
Training data generation services: Services for generating, augmenting, and validating training and test data for AI systems, including synthetic data creation, simulation environments, data quality validation, and human feedback pipelines used for model training, tuning, and evaluation.
Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) services: Structured short-term (4–6 week) embedded engagements to design AI agent architectures and orchestration workflows, covering system blueprints, integration with enterprise data and applications, and governance model alignment.
AI assurance and red-teaming services: Structured engagements to validate AI models and agentic systems for performance, safety, and compliance, including adversarial testing (prompt injection, hallucination, data leakage), bias evaluation, and governance validation.
Please indicate which Responsible AI (RAI) capabilities your organization provides. Focus on capabilities related to AI governance, risk management, compliance, security, and trust, and avoid repeating generic AI services listed above
Definition:
Standalone RAI strategy and advisory services: Advisory services focused on AI risk assessment, use-case classification, and regulatory and governance alignment across predictive AI, Gen AI, and agentic systems
RAI guardrails, policy enforcement, and governance frameworks: Proprietary solutions and frameworks that enforce policies, safety controls, and governance rules across AI model behavior, Gen AI outputs, and agent actions
Model and agent assurance, monitoring, and risk management services: Services for pre- and post-deployment validation, testing, and continuous monitoring of AI models and agents to manage performance, bias, drift, and safety risks
Transparency, auditability, and incident management solutions: Capabilities that provide explainability, end-to-end logging, audit trails, and incident response mechanisms, including overrides and rollback for AI systems
Data protection and privacy controls: Controls and services for protecting sensitive data across AI pipelines, including Personally Identifiable Information (PII) detection, data isolation, residency enforcement, and access management
Please describe the characteristics of the human–AI agent pod-based delivery model, including its pod composition, commercial model, primary functions supported, and typical engagement timeline.
Have you developed partner-specific (SAP, Salesforce, or ServiceNow) AI platforms or layers that enable partners to build, extend, or deploy AI workflows on top of your platform?
What percentage of your Gen AI projects in the past 12 months included building proprietary foundational models for enterprise clients?
What are the various commercial models that you offer to your clients?
Please select all the options that are applicable (percentage figures should add up to 100%).
What is the split between open-source (such as Llama 3.0) and third-party LLMs (such as GPT-4) leveraged in your Gen AI implementations?
Please provide details of enterprise AI implementations delivered by your organization over the past 12–24 months. For each AI category below, indicate the total number of client engagements, the share currently in proof of concept (POC) or pilot stage, and the top five business use cases addressed.
Please provide details of your organization’s initiatives in emerging AI technologies.
Please provide details about your organization’s innovation labs supporting AI.
Client and project details
Please provide the total number of your AI clients across different industry verticals.
How many forward-deployed engineers you have in your organization, and what is your target headcount for the next fiscal year?
Definition: Forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) are customer-facing AI professionals who combine expertise in AI technologies, software engineering, enterprise systems, domain processes, and business functions to design, integrate, customize, and deploy AI solutions.

Please provide the percentage split of your enterprise AI projects across the following areas mentioned: 
Definitions:
Business process optimization: Includes content generation, summarization, classification, sentiment analysis, and so on
New revenue stream creation: Includes creating new data monetization capabilities, such as subscription-based offerings for clients using generative AI, which are revenue-generating for them, such as Adobe Firefly, Grammarly generative AI features, and so on
Please share innovative use cases that demonstrate the differentiating capabilities of your AI practice in the past 12 months. 
Please limit the description of each case study to under 500 characters.
Does your organization provide contractual liability, indemnification, or risk-sharing provisions for AI engagements? If yes, please briefly describe the scope of liability, the types of AI engagements covered, and any limitations or conditions typically applied. (Please limit answer to under 1,000 characters)
For every 1% reduction in delivery effort achieved through AI, what percentage of incremental revenue, project volume, or service demand is being generated? 
Please identify your top five proprietary AI platforms, solutions, or accelerators that are commercially licensed or sold separately from broader managed AI services engagements. For each offering, provide a brief description, pricing model, and estimated contribution to AI-related revenue.
Practice revenue details
What is the total revenue from your AI practice and your year-over-year (YOY) growth rate in the 12 months up to June 30, 2026?
Please indicate how your applied AI revenue is split between different industry verticals.
Please provide percentages that add up to 100%.
Human capital overview
Please provide the head count and the number of delivery support centers for applied AI.
Please list key AI, automation-related certifications held by your workforce, along with their respective certified head counts. Include certifications across LLMs, agentic AI, orchestration platforms, and automation technologies.
Examples:  NVIDIA Certified Generative AI LLM Developer, Databricks Certified Generative AI Engineer Associate, Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Engineer Associate, Google Cloud Generative AI Engineer Certification, Claude Certified Architect – Foundations (Anthropic)
Please provide a unique head count for each certification. The total certified head count across all AI and automation certifications should not exceed your total employee strength for the current year.
Industry ecosystem overview
Please provide the details of the partner ecosystem for AI in your organization.
Please provide the names of your top 10 partners and the value-add they provide to your AI practice.
Strategy and investment plans
Please describe your organization’s growth strategy for the next 12 months.
You may choose to cover topics such as plans around new service offerings, partnership strategy, practice expansion into new markets, enhancing capabilities in advanced technologies, patents filed, new hiring and training initiatives, and revenue goals. 
Please provide a brief response, preferably in bullet points, under 1,500 characters.
Please indicate the budget for planned investments in the applied AI space over the next 12 months (in USD million).
Please list all the prototype solutions related to AI to be commercialized over the next 12 months.
Please limit the description of each solution to under 500 characters.
Indicate the percentage split of your AI investments over the next 12 months across the categories mentioned below. Percentages must total 100%. (Please provide a brief response, preferably in bullet points, under 1,000 characters):
Deterministic and predictive AI: Rule-based automation, RPA, and classical ML models orchestrated for structured and repeatable workflows
Generative and agentic AI: LLMs, multimodal models, and AI agents orchestrated for dynamic decisioning, autonomous execution, and multistep workflow coordination
Please describe the distribution of your planned investment among different activities.
Please provide indicative percentages that add up to 100%.
Please provide details of any AI-related acquisitions that your organization has made in the past 12 months.
Additional information
We strongly recommend uploading additional documents related to your applied AI services capabilities and strategy.  
Please note that you can upload a single file of up to 100MB. So, in case you wish to share multiple files, please zip them into one file to upload.

~40% faster decision-making (300+ mortgage-specific concepts embedded)

Defining applied AI services

Applied AI services comprise consulting, engineering, implementation, integration, and managed services that help enterprises embed AI capabilities into applications, workflows, and business processes. The scope includes the application of deterministic AI, generative AI, and agentic AI capabilities across enterprise environments to improve operational efficiency, enhance customer experiences, and enable new revenue opportunities. It also includes forward-looking AI paradigms, including neuromorphic AI, physical AI, and quantum AI.

input: How is Kairos OS framed as domain-specific agentic AI with gain-share BPS GTM?
expected_output:
Kairos OS is framed as an AI operating system built inside an operations business, not a lab, using 25 years of domain expertise across healthcare, BFS, and CXM. Its domain specificity comes from the Domain Harness, Intelligent Context Framework, and prebuilt agentic workflow blueprints for use cases like prior authorisation, fraud triage, collections, and fulfilment.

Its BPS GTM is gain-share and outcome-led: Kairos Level 2 and Level 3 engagements use outcome-linked SLAs, gain-share provisions, and retainer-plus-outcomes bonus models, with Firstsource underwriting delivery performance. In short, it positions agentic AI as production-grade, domain-led operations transformation tied to measurable business results rather than FTE-based delivery.

Kairos uses a five-layer intelligence stack to connect enterprise data to AI-native operations and deliver outcomes-linked transformation.

1. **Systems of Record**: Raw data and transactions from CRM, billing, field service, collections, and other core systems.

input: If CRMs/ERPs/EHRs log transactions but miss exceptions/why, what org issues would ICF prevent?
expected_output:
ICF helps prevent several organizational issues caused by missing decision context:

- **Knowledge loss:** It preserves tribal knowledge, rationale, exceptions, and approvals that would otherwise disappear when experts leave.
- **Repeated mistakes:** Teams can reason from searchable precedent instead of reinventing decisions or repeating past errors.
- **Slow onboarding:** New hires get access to queryable SOPs and prior resolutions, reducing ramp-up time.
- **Inconsistent decisions:** It captures the **what, why, who, and how** behind actions, improving exception handling consistency.
- **AI escalation and context blindness:** It gives AI agents the context traditional systems miss, reducing escalations caused by missing context.
- **Compliance and continuity risk:** Nuanced compliance interpretations and operational logic remain preserved even through turnover.
- **Revenue leakage from disconnected context:** By linking decisions and exceptions across systems, it reduces losses caused by fragmented information.
