input: If a payor adopts Firstsource AI, how would Kairos run end-to-end payer ops?
expected_output:
Kairos would run payer operations as an AI-native operating model where AI agents, copilots, and human associates work as one accountable workforce across the full value chain — including claims, member and provider service, prior authorization, appeals and grievances, provider data, payment integrity, and quality workflows.

In practice, Kairos serves as the operating layer that combines:
- payer-specific skills, playbooks, and guardrails through its Domain Harness,
- contextual intelligence from claims, member, provider, contract, and clinical data through the Intelligent Context Framework,
- orchestration across workflows and enterprise systems,
- governance through traceability, access controls, and Progressive Trust oversight.

End to end, it would:
- ingest and classify documents, calls, emails, and digital intake,
- extract and summarize key information,
- create and route cases,
- prioritize work using propensity models and operational signals,
- support or automate decisions in claims, prior auth, appeals, and service workflows,
- write back into core systems through governed APIs,
- monitor quality, compliance, drift, and outcomes continuously.

The model is not “AI as a point tool”; it is “Intelligence that Operates,” meaning Kairos is designed to actively operate work end-to-end with accountability. Firstsource’s roadmap is to expand these Kairos-enabled workflows over the next 18 months, scale more agentic payer operations, and move selected workflows to higher autonomy tiers under structured human oversight.
context:
AI in Healthcare Payor
What is your organization's AI strategy for the Healthcare Payor vertical — including your AI vision, target use cases, and 18-month roadmap? (Describe your overarching AI vision for the Healthcare Payor vertical, your top 3–5 priority use cases, and key milestones planned over the next 6, 12, and 18 months.)
Firstsource’s AI strategy for the healthcare payer vertical is anchored in Intelligence that Operates — our commitment to encode deep payer domain expertise into AI that does not merely advise or automate, but actively operates work end-to-end with accountability. This strategy is delivered through Kairos, our operating system for AI-native operations, which is the dominant architectural and operating construct across our payer AI portfolio. Around Kairos, we combine payer platforms, AI partners, process intelligence tools, and reusable accelerators so that every deployment compounds operational knowledge rather than remaining a standalone point solution. The response that follows sets out our AI vision for the payer vertical, our priority use cases for the next eighteen months, the engagement model through which we deliver, the milestones we are targeting over the next 6, 12, and 18 months, and the governance and outcome-accountability principles that underpin the model.
AI Vision for the Healthcare Payor Vertical
Firstsource’s AI vision for healthcare payers is to operate the payer value chain — claims, customer service, member engagement, care management, provider data and network management, payment integrity, and quality and regulatory workflows — as an AI-native operating model in which AI agents, copilots, and human associates work as one accountable workforce. This vision is expressly delivered through Kairos, which serves as the dominant operating environment for payer workflows by combining payer-specific skills and guardrails, contextual intelligence drawn from client systems and domain knowledge, and operational signals from process, task, document, and conversation intelligence. The result is a payer operating model where regulatory exposure, member experience, medical-cost performance, and workforce productivity improve together rather than in isolation, and where every new deployment strengthens the Kairos operating layer for subsequent payer engagements.
Top Priority Use Cases (next 18 months)
Agentic claims adjudication and Late Payment Interest (LPI) prevention — combining Claims Agentic AI workflows, propensity models, and operational sensors to identify high-risk claims early, prioritize work intelligently, and reduce late-payment exposure.
Sympraxis® Communication Hub expansion across appeals and grievances, prior authorization, and provider correspondence — converting unstructured payer intake into structured downstream action with automated classification, summarization, extraction, routing, and case creation.
Member experience transformation through Member Outreach, Benefit Inquiry, conversational AI, QA/QC, and customer-service agentic workflows — improving response times, digital containment, and service quality across member and provider interactions.
Provider data and contract intelligence — AI-powered classification, extraction, validation, and workflow support across provider onboarding, contracting, directory quality, and network administration.
Risk adjustment, quality, and care-gap optimization — through Risk Adjustment Copilot, Care Gap Reviews, Prior Authorization Copilot, and related clinical-document summarization workflows to improve accuracy, timeliness, and quality outcomes.
Payment integrity at scale — combining Claims & Payment Integrity Copilot, Integrity 360, and process intelligence to improve audit productivity, reduce leakage, and strengthen recovery performance.
Engagement Model
Firstsource delivers every engagement through a structured three-stage motion — Transform, Implement, and Operate — as a single continuous programme under one contract, supported by three commercial entry points calibrated to client ambition and readiness. Level 1 Discover is a four-week, fixed-fee AI and operations maturity assessment that benchmarks the payer against vertical peers and produces a board-ready transformation business case. Level 2 Explore and Expand is a 90-day, outcomes-linked deployment that puts the first AI-powered payer process into production within 90 days. Level 3 Propel is a 12-month retainer with an outcomes bonus, supported by a named Kairos Lead accountable for quarterly board-level outcome reviews and continuous optimisation across the deployed footprint.
6-Month Milestones
Expand Kairos-enabled payer workflows across additional claims, service, and intake use cases, with selected skills progressing to higher-autonomy tiers under structured human oversight.
Scale healthcare-payer-focused AI and technology lab activity around claims, intake, service, and clinical workflow use cases, including co-innovation with anchor clients.
Advance production deployment of LPI, communication-hub, and provider-data intelligence use cases with stronger traceability, monitoring, and governance instrumentation.
12-Month Milestones
Launch additional Kairos-enabled payer skills and benchmarks across claims, payment integrity, service, and care workflows to support more repeatable transformation starts.
Scale Agentic AI Studio, Claims Agentic AI Workflow, Customer Service Agentic AI Workflow, QA/QC Copilot, and training copilots from pilot and anchor deployments into broader production usage.
Advance prior-authorization, clinical summarization, risk-adjustment, and care-gap workflows under structured human oversight, aligned to payer policy and regulatory requirements.
Extend payer interoperability and workflow integration to support broader digital intake, service, and adjudication use cases at scale.
18-Month Milestones
Scale Kairos-enabled agentic payer operations across a broader portfolio of outcome-linked engagements, with named delivery leaders accountable for measurable improvement.
Further productize AI-led payment integrity, quality, and service offerings using reusable Kairos skills, operational context, and payer-specific accelerators.
Expand the Kairos ecosystem across hyperscalers, specialist AI partners, BPaaS platforms, and system-integration partnerships to support greater deployment choice and scale.
Governance and Outcome Accountability
Governance is architected into the operating model rather than bolted on after the fact. Our Progressive Trust approach calibrates AI autonomy through staged human oversight, with skills progressing only after evidence of stable performance, quality, and compliance. Domain-specific guardrails, access controls, traceability, and responsible-AI review are embedded into Kairos-enabled workflows, and outcome accountability is expressed commercially through fixed-fee, outcome-linked, and value-oriented models depending on client maturity and scope. The combination — Intelligence that Operates, delivered through Kairos, governed through progressive oversight, and tied to measurable business outcomes — is how Firstsource differentiates as a payer digital services partner.
Do you have a dedicated Healthcare Payor AI Center of Excellence (CoE)? Describe its structure, headcount, and mandate. (Indicate whether the CoE is standalone or shared across verticals, total FTE headcount, reporting structure, and its top 3 mandates for 2026. If no CoE exists, state whether one is planned and by when.)
Yes — Firstsource supports the Healthcare Payor practice through a payer-focused AI capability embedded within our broader Innovation Network. The model combines payer domain depth with shared AI, data, automation, and process-intelligence platform investments, with Kairos serving as the dominant architectural backbone for how we design, deploy, govern, and scale AI in payer environments. This allows payer-specific innovation to benefit from firm-wide engineering and governance while keeping domain logic, workflows, and operational priorities healthcare-payer focused.
Structure and Positioning
The payer AI capability sits within the Healthcare Solutions practice and draws on shared Kairos platform investments across agentic orchestration, contextual intelligence, process and task intelligence, and responsible AI governance.
Day-to-day delivery is supported through payer-focused AI and technology lab activity spanning claims, intake, service, quality, and care workflows, with domain SMEs, AI engineers, automation specialists, analytics teams, and operations practitioners working together.
Headcount and Composition
The payer AI capability draws on a dedicated mix of AI, data-science, and AI-enabling FTEs organised across operations engineering, domain harness engineering, data science and MLOps, conversational AI, and clinical oversight.
Operations Engineers refine payer playbooks, policies, and guardrails from execution signals captured through Kairos-enabled workflows and contextual intelligence.
Domain Harness Engineers build, test, and promote payer-domain skills and guardrails to production within the Kairos operating environment.
Data scientists and MLOps engineers support propensity, NLP, and decision models across claims, payment integrity, risk adjustment, and care management.
Conversational AI specialists support voice, chat, and virtual-agent deployments across member and provider service operations.
Clinician reviewers and AI-safety reviewers include registered nurses and physicians from the TeleMedik acquisition, bringing a 380+ member URAC-accredited clinical workforce with all-50-state reach to support regulated clinical and utilization workflows under Human-in-the-Loop oversight.
This payer-focused capability is complemented by a broader bench of AI-certified professionals, automation engineers, process-mining specialists, analytics teams, trainers, and healthcare operations experts across the firm. The wider enterprise AI and Digital Services organization supports the payer practice with reusable accelerators, engineering standards, lab infrastructure, and training programs, including AI-powered enablement that has reduced time-to-proficiency and improved quality in operational teams.
Reporting Structure
The capability is governed through Healthcare Solutions leadership in coordination with the broader AI, technology, and governance functions that support Kairos-enabled delivery. Oversight is reinforced through regular leadership reviews, solution-governance checkpoints, and client-facing outcome reviews for strategic engagements.
Top Three Mandates for 2026
Productize and scale Kairos-enabled payer skills and accelerators across claims, service, payment integrity, provider data, and care workflows so that each new engagement starts from reusable domain assets rather than a blank sheet.
Expand payer benchmarks, contextual intelligence, and operational-signal frameworks to strengthen prioritization, traceability, and measurable improvement for clients.
Graduate additional Kairos-enabled workflows to higher autonomy tiers under structured oversight, while extending responsible-AI controls, monitoring, and deployment discipline across the portfolio.
All CoE activity is conducted under our Responsible AI policy framework, aligned to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and EU AI Act Article 10 and 11 requirements, with clinical-safety and regulatory guardrails embedded directly into every Domain Harness skill rather than overlaid as after-the-fact controls.
What is your AI operating model for payor clients — build, buy, partner, or hybrid? Which AI platforms/foundational models do you leverage (e.g., Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex)? (State whether your model is build, buy, partner, or hybrid, and list the specific AI platforms and foundational models used for Healthcare Payor clients with a brief rationale for your approach.)
Hybrid by design. Firstsource builds the layers of the AI stack that compound into proprietary, payer-specific IP; partners on the layers where hyperscaler and platform economics favor scale; and licenses best-in-class specialist solutions where domain-specific platforms are already strong reference points. This is a deliberate architectural choice that protects client value over time, and within this model Kairos serves as the operating environment that ties proprietary skills, contextual intelligence, orchestration, and governance together.
Operating Model — Kairos-led Build, Partner, and License
Built components — the durable, payer-specific IP that compounds with every engagement and is orchestrated through Kairos as the dominant operating system for payer AI:
The Domain Harness part of the Kairos architecture— encoding 25+ years of payer expertise as executable skills, playbooks, and guardrails.
The Intelligent Context Framework (ICF) — capturing canonical member, provider, claim, contract, and clinical entity context, with Decision Traces preserving the full causal chain of every AI-assisted decision.
Operations Intelligence sensors — Process Mining, Object-Centric Process Mining, Task Mining, Conversation Intelligence, Knowledge Mining, and Document Intelligence — surfacing in-flight signal across payer operations.
A growing portfolio of proprietary copilots and agentic workflows, including the Claims and Payment Integrity Copilot, the Claims Agentic AI Workflow, the Customer Service Agentic AI Workflow, the Prior Authorisation Copilot, the Risk Adjustment Copilot, the Care Gap Reviews Copilot, the SARA Instructional Design Copilot, and the WFM Real-Time Adherence Copilot.
Partnered components — the scale layers that plug into Kairos where hyperscaler and platform economics favor broader ecosystem leverage:
Foundational large language models, accessed through hyperscaler enterprise agreements rather than direct model contracts — detailed in the section that follows.
Vector databases, embedding stores, and retrieval infrastructure (Pinecone, OpenSearch, Neo4j).
Hyperscaler infrastructure — Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, and Google Cloud — chosen per engagement to align with the client's preferred cloud.
Licensed components — best-in-class specialist platforms that extend the Kairos operating environment in domains where niche vendors hold the strongest reference capability:
Celonis for Object-Centric Process Mining, Soroco Scout for Task Mining, and HiLabs for healthcare-specific data quality.
Lyzr Agent Studio and Opus Applied AI for agentic workflow orchestration accelerators.
Codoxo and Edifecs for encounter and fraud-waste-abuse submission workflows; Andros for provider credentialing; Simplify Healthcare for network management; Ribbon Health and Perspecta for provider directory data quality.
Foundational Models in Production for Payer Clients
Model selection is made per skill, per client, and per deployment environment rather than as a single firm-wide standard, allowing us to align with each client’s preferred cloud, regulatory posture, and cost-performance requirements. In practice, we leverage enterprise AI ecosystems across Microsoft Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, and Meta/Llama-based ecosystems, alongside specialist AI platforms and open-source tooling where appropriate. Kairos is intentionally model-agnostic: payer skills, context, orchestration, and governance persist independently of whichever foundation model is selected for a given workflow.
Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service — GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, and GPT-4 Turbo — used for the majority of Generative AI workloads under our enterprise Microsoft partnership.
Amazon Web Services Bedrock — Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Claude 3.5 Haiku, and Meta Llama 3 — used for client environments standardised on AWS.
Google Vertex AI — Gemini 1.5 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Flash — used for select engagements, including clients standardised on Google Cloud.
Open-weight models such as Meta Llama 3 and Mistral — fine-tuned and hosted privately for narrowly scoped, high-volume tasks where unit hosting cost is the binding constraint and the workload is well-defined enough to specialise the model.
Specialty Models and AI Capabilities
Beyond foundational language models, we deploy specialty models and frameworks for targeted capabilities such as semantic retrieval, transcription, intent classification, propensity scoring, summarization, document understanding, and workflow orchestration. These are selected according to the use case — for example, payer-document retrieval, contact-center interaction analysis, claims risk scoring, or process-intelligence monitoring — and are composed through Kairos so that domain-specific logic and contextual intelligence remain stable even when underlying models or tools evolve.
Cohere Embed and the OpenAI embedding family for semantic retrieval over payer documents, SOPs, contracts, and clinical guidelines.
OpenAI Whisper for batch transcription; AssemblyAI for real-time transcription in contact-centre and clinical-triage interactions.
XGBoost and DistilBERT for in-house risk-propensity, intent-classification, and Late Payment Interest (LPI) propensity-scoring models.
LangGraph and Temporal for durable agent orchestration; MCP (Model Context Protocol) for structured tool and data integration.
Rationale — Kairos as the durable, model-agnostic operating layer
Kairos is deliberately model-agnostic. Following our first agentic design tenet — separate Brain, Hands, and Memory — the reasoning layer (Brain), the skill library (Hands), and the durable context (Memory) are kept as independent, loosely coupled components. The Domain Harness, part of the Kairos Architecture, the Intelligent Context Framework, and the skill libraries persist as Firstsource and client IP regardless of which foundational model provides reasoning at any given moment. We are able to swap models skill-by-skill, client-by-client, and region-by-region without rewriting our domain assets, which protects clients from vendor lock-in, foundational-model pricing volatility, and the accelerating pace of model deprecation. Equally important, it ensures that 25+ years of payer domain expertise continues to compound inside the durable layers Firstsource owns and operates, rather than inside the foundational models we rent.

Within Kairos, our AI capabilities are organised as a portfolio of deep-domain technology assets and accelerators — pre-built platforms, frameworks, models, and solution accelerators built specifically for HealthTech, FinTech, and CXTech contexts. This portfolio gives our delivery teams a coherent set of reusable components, over one hundred proprietary copilots, decision agents, knowledge graphs, and accelerators, to compose into client-specific solutions, rather than building each engagement from first principles.

Integration surface
Our agents do not operate in isolation. They integrate natively with the client's existing payor estate — core administrative platforms (Facets, QNXT, Proclaim, PowerMHS, HealthRules Payer), CRM systems (Salesforce, AWS Connect), payment integrity tools (UiPath, Zelis, MPX, ClaimShark, Codoxo, Autonomize.AI), document and intake systems (Sympraxis, OCR/ICR pipelines), and BPaaS partner platforms (HealthEdge, mPulse, Edifecs, Reveleer). Agents read from and write to these systems through secure, governed APIs, ensuring that every action is traceable back to the calling agent and the underlying decision logic.
How we govern autonomy
Agentic AI introduces operational risk that copilots and traditional automation do not. Firstsource addresses this risk through three reinforcing layers of governance.
Principle-based governance. Every deployment is evaluated against eight standards — fairness, AI for good, regulatory compliance, accountability, interpretability, privacy and security, inclusiveness, and reliability. These principles translate into concrete acceptance criteria during model validation and into ongoing monitoring once a workflow is deployed.
Autonomy calibration through Progressive Trust. We do not deploy agents at full autonomy from day one. Every workflow begins under Human-in-the-Loop review at every decision, where the agent's output is approved or corrected before any downstream action is taken. As we accumulate evidence of sustained accuracy on a defined task, we graduate the workflow to Human-on-the-Loop, where the human supervises the agent's actions rather than approving each one. Only low-risk, high-confidence task domains progress to Human-above-the-Loop autonomy, and continuous post-hoc audit is maintained even at that level. This progression keeps our risk posture conservative and allows us to demonstrate compliance to regulators and clients alike.
Platform-level technical control. Lyzr provides reflection-based validation, groundedness checks against enterprise knowledge sources, fairness and bias safeguards, toxicity monitoring, automated PII detection and redaction, and token-level audit logs. Opus enforces compliance tracking and embeds explicit human review checkpoints at every workflow step.
Underlying all of this, our infrastructure is certified to ISO 27001, HITRUST, SOC 2 Type 2, and HIPAA. Business Associate Agreements cover every client engagement. A 24/7 Security Operations Center, operated in partnership with PwC on Microsoft Sentinel SIEM, monitors continuously across our environment.
Sympraxis as the intake and case-orchestration backbone
Several of the agentic deployments described below are integrated with Sympraxis® Health Plan Communication Hub — Firstsource intake and case-orchestration platform, deployed for 15 payor clients. Sympraxis ingests provider and member documents from multiple intake channels (mail, fax, portals, EDI), automates document classification, data extraction, summarization, and case creation through GenAI and OCR/ICR pipelines, and routes work into downstream queues. While Sympraxis itself is intelligent document processing rather than fully autonomous agentic execution, it provides the agentic triage and routing layer on which our downstream autonomous agents operate.

Responsible AI capabilities
Compliance with CMS and HIPAA for AI-driven decisions
For AI-driven decisions in payor environments, regulatory compliance is enforced at three layers: technical control, process control, and human authority.
At the technical layer, our infrastructure is certified to HIPAA, HITRUST CSF, SOC 2 Type 2, and ISO 27001, with Business Associate Agreements covering every payor client engagement. Encryption, access controls, audit logging, and breach notification capabilities meet or exceed HIPAA Security Rule requirements. For AI-specific governance, our control environment is aligned to ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management systems) and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.
At the process layer, we map each AI deployment to applicable federal and state regulations during use-case design. For prior authorization deployments specifically, our agents are designed to comply with the CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule (CMS-0057-F), including the timeliness mandates that took effect in January 2026. For deployments touching Medicare Advantage coverage decisions, our agents are configured in line with CMS guidance that algorithms and AI models cannot be the sole basis for a coverage or medical necessity determination clinical reviewers retain authority, and AI outputs serve as decision support, not decision-making. Section 1557 non-discrimination requirements are reflected in our fairness testing protocols, and 21st Century Cures Act information-blocking obligations are addressed in our data access patterns.
At the human authority layer, every AI-driven decision that affects a member or provider coverage, payment, authorization, or appeals outcome — is either reviewed by a qualified human or governed by a Progressive Trust autonomy level that has been explicitly authorized by the client. Clinical decisions remain the responsibility of credentialed clinicians; payment decisions remain the responsibility of qualified claims professionals. AI accelerates and informs these decisions; it does not replace the regulated decision-maker.
Firstsource treats Responsible AI not as a policy document, but as an operating model. Every agentic and generative AI deployment in our payor portfolio operates under the same eight-principle Kairos Responsible AI framework, the same Progressive Trust calibration, the same platform-level controls, and the same multi-tier governance ownership. Regulatory compliance with CMS, HIPAA, Section 1557, and state-level requirements are enforced through technical certification, process design, and human authority working together. As regulatory expectations around AI in healthcare continue to evolve, including the CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule and emerging state-level AI accountability legislation, our governance framework is designed to absorb new requirements without disrupting client operations.

What is your AI governance framework for payor clients — including model validation, drift monitoring, audit trails, and rollback mechanisms? (Describe the governance components in place — such as model validation, drift monitoring, audit trails, rollback mechanisms, and governance boards — including the frequency of each activity, who approves models before deployment, how incidents are escalated, and what the rollback SLA is.)
Our AI governance framework for payor clients is designed to make Intelligence that Operates safe, auditable, and production-ready. Kairos acts as the governance operating layer as much as the orchestration layer: it enforces deployment gates, captures traceability, calibrates autonomy through Progressive Trust, and supports rollback when performance or policy conditions require it.
Core governance components
Model validation: design review, data-lineage review, offline validation, fairness and error analysis, and workflow acceptance testing before pilot or production.
Autonomy calibration: workflows begin under Human-in-the-Loop oversight and graduate only after sustained performance and explicit sign-off.
Drift monitoring: production monitoring covers accuracy, confidence, throughput, exceptions, fairness signals, and input-distribution drift.
Audit trails: model version, workflow version, data access, decision path, overrides, and downstream actions are recorded and searchable.
Rollback and incident response: material failures trigger containment, root-cause analysis, rollback to a known-good version or manual fallback, client notification, and documented remediation.
Validation occurs before every material release. Monitoring is typically weekly during stabilization and monthly or quarterly in steady state, depending on risk. Rollback SLAs are defined by use case; for higher-risk workflows, fallback to a prior model or manual mode is typically targeted within hours, not days.
How do you manage data privacy and security when training or fine-tuning AI models on payor member/claims data? (Describe the data privacy controls in place — such as de-identification, synthetic data generation, federated learning, or HIPAA BAAs — including where payor data is stored during training, who has access, how consent and authorization are managed, and any certifications or third-party audits that validate your data privacy posture.)
When training or fine-tuning AI on payor member or claims data, we apply a privacy-by-design model. The starting principle is to use the least sensitive data required, prefer retrieval-grounded or configuration-driven approaches where possible, and where training is required, apply de-identification, access control, contractual controls, and auditable operating procedures throughout the lifecycle. This is managed through Kairos so that data handling, model promotion, and runtime usage remain governed under one operating model.
Core controls
De-identification: Safe Harbor or Expert Determination methods where appropriate; for many GenAI workflows we prefer RAG over broad fine-tuning on raw PHI.
Data minimization: only the minimum fields needed for the task are used; retention is defined by client contract and governance policy.
Logical segregation and access control: client data is segregated by client and environment; access is least-privilege, role-based, logged, and reviewed.
Secure storage and transfer: encryption in transit and at rest, governed environments, and auditable access pathways.
Contractual controls: BAAs, client-approved processing terms, audit rights, and incident-response obligations.
Training and tuning datasets are stored in client-approved cloud or enterprise environments aligned to regulatory and residency requirements. Access is restricted to authorized delivery, engineering, data science, and governance personnel on a documented need-to-know basis, and all access is auditable.

We maintain governance processes designed for the possibility of model failure, performance degradation, or bias drift in payor environments. This response is built into Kairos and reinforced through Progressive Trust governance.
Standard response pattern
Detection: alerts, override patterns, QA sampling, fairness checks, client feedback, or exception spikes.
Containment: move to Human-in-the-Loop or manual fallback.
Root-cause analysis: determine whether the issue arose from data drift, policy change, prompt or retrieval error, model degradation, or workflow integration error.
Remediation: recalibration, data refresh, policy update, routing change, model rollback, or additional human review gates.
Disclosure and learning: notify the client per governance terms and feed the lessons back into validation thresholds, monitoring, and deployment standards.

2 | Explainability and interpretability | Every AI-driven decision is accompanied by a human-readable rationale citing the inputs considered, the logic applied, the supporting policy or guideline, and the confidence level. | SHAP for feature attribution; decision-trail logging; model cards documenting training data, validation results, intended use, and known limitations; natural-language rationale generation for clinical and operational reviewers. | For prior authorization agents, every auto-approval or auto-denial carries a structured explanation citing the relevant payer policy section, clinical guideline, and the specific evidence extracted from the medical record. Reviewers see the same explanation on escalated cases under Human-in-the-Loop, ensuring consistent reasoning across human and AI decisions.
3 | Auditability and traceability | Every agent action, model prediction, data access, and human override is logged with full context — input, decision, confidence, supporting evidence, timestamp, agent or user identity — and retained per client record-retention requirements. | Lyzr token-level audit logs; Opus compliance tracking; immutable append-only audit trails; structured event logs ingested into client and Firstsource SIEM systems; annual third-party audit of the AI control environment. | All AI decisions on payor accounts are retained for the duration required by client record-retention policies (typically seven to ten years for healthcare records). Firstsource makes full audit trails available to clients and regulators on request, searchable by case ID, member ID, provider ID, agent name, and decision type, enabling rapid response to compliance inquiries, internal audits, and regulatory examinations without operational disruption.
4 | Privacy and data protection | Member and claims data flows are protected end-to-end by de-identification where possible, encryption, role-based access, and contractual safeguards. | Automated PII detection and redaction (Lyzr); de-identification under HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination methods; AES-256 encryption at rest; TLS 1.2+ in transit; client-managed or Firstsource HSM-managed encryption keys per client preference. | Training data is de-identified before any model fine-tuning. Production data flows are governed by client-specific Business Associate Agreements. Access follows the minimum necessary standard with audit trails on every access event. Data residency is configurable per client requirements (US-only deployments where mandated).
5 | Human oversight (Progressive Trust) | No agent is deployed at full autonomy from day one. Workflows graduate from Human-in-the-Loop to Human-on-the-Loop to Human-above-the-Loop only after sustained accuracy, bias-test pass, and client sign-off. | Lyzr workflow gates; Opus human checkpoints; Progressive Trust framework documented per deployment; quarterly autonomy reviews. | Every new agentic deployment for a payor client begins under Human-in-the-Loop review on every decision. Graduation requires a minimum 90-day stabilization period, sustained accuracy above the contracted threshold, bias-check pass, and explicit client sign-off documented in the engagement record.
6 | Drift monitoring and model performance | Continuous monitoring of model accuracy, prediction confidence, input distribution drift, and output quality, with thresholds that trigger retraining or rollback. | Lyzr monitoring; Opus performance tracking; client-facing model performance dashboards; configurable alert thresholds; automated retraining pipelines. | Model performance is reviewed weekly during stabilization and monthly in steady state. Drift exceeding thresholds triggers root-cause analysis, recalibration, or rollback to a known-good model version within a contracted SLA (typically four hours for material drift).
7 | Incident response and rollback | Structured response to AI failures, unintended outputs, or bias incidents — containment, root-cause analysis, remediation, client disclosure, regulatory notification where applicable, and post-mortem. | Documented incident playbooks per deployment; rollback to prior model version under contracted SLA; client notification protocol; remediation tracking in our governance system. | Every deployment has a documented rollback SLA and an incident response playbook approved by both Firstsource Compliance and the client. Material incidents are disclosed to the client and, where applicable, to regulators within the timelines required by HIPAA Breach Notification and state law. Post-incident reviews drive model and process updates.

context:
AI in Healthcare Payor
What is your organization's AI strategy for the Healthcare Payor vertical — including your AI vision, target use cases, and 18-month roadmap? (Describe your overarching AI vision for the Healthcare Payor vertical, your top 3–5 priority use cases, and key milestones planned over the next 6, 12, and 18 months.)
Firstsource’s AI strategy for the healthcare payer vertical is anchored in Intelligence that Operates — our commitment to encode deep payer domain expertise into AI that does not merely advise or automate, but actively operates work end-to-end with accountability. This strategy is delivered through Kairos, our operating system for AI-native operations, which is the dominant architectural and operating construct across our payer AI portfolio. Around Kairos, we combine payer platforms, AI partners, process intelligence tools, and reusable accelerators so that every deployment compounds operational knowledge rather than remaining a standalone point solution. The response that follows sets out our AI vision for the payer vertical, our priority use cases for the next eighteen months, the engagement model through which we deliver, the milestones we are targeting over the next 6, 12, and 18 months, and the governance and outcome-accountability principles that underpin the model.
AI Vision for the Healthcare Payor Vertical
Firstsource’s AI vision for healthcare payers is to operate the payer value chain — claims, customer service, member engagement, care management, provider data and network management, payment integrity, and quality and regulatory workflows — as an AI-native operating model in which AI agents, copilots, and human associates work as one accountable workforce. This vision is expressly delivered through Kairos, which serves as the dominant operating environment for payer workflows by combining payer-specific skills and guardrails, contextual intelligence drawn from client systems and domain knowledge, and operational signals from process, task, document, and conversation intelligence. The result is a payer operating model where regulatory exposure, member experience, medical-cost performance, and workforce productivity improve together rather than in isolation, and where every new deployment strengthens the Kairos operating layer for subsequent payer engagements.
Top Priority Use Cases (next 18 months)
Agentic claims adjudication and Late Payment Interest (LPI) prevention — combining Claims Agentic AI workflows, propensity models, and operational sensors to identify high-risk claims early, prioritize work intelligently, and reduce late-payment exposure.
Sympraxis® Communication Hub expansion across appeals and grievances, prior authorization, and provider correspondence — converting unstructured payer intake into structured downstream action with automated classification, summarization, extraction, routing, and case creation.
Member experience transformation through Member Outreach, Benefit Inquiry, conversational AI, QA/QC, and customer-service agentic workflows — improving response times, digital containment, and service quality across member and provider interactions.
Provider data and contract intelligence — AI-powered classification, extraction, validation, and workflow support across provider onboarding, contracting, directory quality, and network administration.
Risk adjustment, quality, and care-gap optimization — through Risk Adjustment Copilot, Care Gap Reviews, Prior Authorization Copilot, and related clinical-document summarization workflows to improve accuracy, timeliness, and quality outcomes.
Payment integrity at scale — combining Claims & Payment Integrity Copilot, Integrity 360, and process intelligence to improve audit productivity, reduce leakage, and strengthen recovery performance.
Engagement Model
Firstsource delivers every engagement through a structured three-stage motion — Transform, Implement, and Operate — as a single continuous programme under one contract, supported by three commercial entry points calibrated to client ambition and readiness. Level 1 Discover is a four-week, fixed-fee AI and operations maturity assessment that benchmarks the payer against vertical peers and produces a board-ready transformation business case. Level 2 Explore and Expand is a 90-day, outcomes-linked deployment that puts the first AI-powered payer process into production within 90 days. Level 3 Propel is a 12-month retainer with an outcomes bonus, supported by a named Kairos Lead accountable for quarterly board-level outcome reviews and continuous optimisation across the deployed footprint.
6-Month Milestones
Expand Kairos-enabled payer workflows across additional claims, service, and intake use cases, with selected skills progressing to higher-autonomy tiers under structured human oversight.
Scale healthcare-payer-focused AI and technology lab activity around claims, intake, service, and clinical workflow use cases, including co-innovation with anchor clients.
Advance production deployment of LPI, communication-hub, and provider-data intelligence use cases with stronger traceability, monitoring, and governance instrumentation.
12-Month Milestones
Launch additional Kairos-enabled payer skills and benchmarks across claims, payment integrity, service, and care workflows to support more repeatable transformation starts.
Scale Agentic AI Studio, Claims Agentic AI Workflow, Customer Service Agentic AI Workflow, QA/QC Copilot, and training copilots from pilot and anchor deployments into broader production usage.
Advance prior-authorization, clinical summarization, risk-adjustment, and care-gap workflows under structured human oversight, aligned to payer policy and regulatory requirements.
Extend payer interoperability and workflow integration to support broader digital intake, service, and adjudication use cases at scale.
18-Month Milestones
Scale Kairos-enabled agentic payer operations across a broader portfolio of outcome-linked engagements, with named delivery leaders accountable for measurable improvement.
Further productize AI-led payment integrity, quality, and service offerings using reusable Kairos skills, operational context, and payer-specific accelerators.
Expand the Kairos ecosystem across hyperscalers, specialist AI partners, BPaaS platforms, and system-integration partnerships to support greater deployment choice and scale.
Governance and Outcome Accountability
Governance is architected into the operating model rather than bolted on after the fact. Our Progressive Trust approach calibrates AI autonomy through staged human oversight, with skills progressing only after evidence of stable performance, quality, and compliance. Domain-specific guardrails, access controls, traceability, and responsible-AI review are embedded into Kairos-enabled workflows, and outcome accountability is expressed commercially through fixed-fee, outcome-linked, and value-oriented models depending on client maturity and scope. The combination — Intelligence that Operates, delivered through Kairos, governed through progressive oversight, and tied to measurable business outcomes — is how Firstsource differentiates as a payer digital services partner.
Do you have a dedicated Healthcare Payor AI Center of Excellence (CoE)? Describe its structure, headcount, and mandate. (Indicate whether the CoE is standalone or shared across verticals, total FTE headcount, reporting structure, and its top 3 mandates for 2026. If no CoE exists, state whether one is planned and by when.)
Yes — Firstsource supports the Healthcare Payor practice through a payer-focused AI capability embedded within our broader Innovation Network. The model combines payer domain depth with shared AI, data, automation, and process-intelligence platform investments, with Kairos serving as the dominant architectural backbone for how we design, deploy, govern, and scale AI in payer environments. This allows payer-specific innovation to benefit from firm-wide engineering and governance while keeping domain logic, workflows, and operational priorities healthcare-payer focused.
Structure and Positioning
The payer AI capability sits within the Healthcare Solutions practice and draws on shared Kairos platform investments across agentic orchestration, contextual intelligence, process and task intelligence, and responsible AI governance.
Day-to-day delivery is supported through payer-focused AI and technology lab activity spanning claims, intake, service, quality, and care workflows, with domain SMEs, AI engineers, automation specialists, analytics teams, and operations practitioners working together.
Headcount and Composition
The payer AI capability draws on a dedicated mix of AI, data-science, and AI-enabling FTEs organised across operations engineering, domain harness engineering, data science and MLOps, conversational AI, and clinical oversight.
Operations Engineers refine payer playbooks, policies, and guardrails from execution signals captured through Kairos-enabled workflows and contextual intelligence.
Domain Harness Engineers build, test, and promote payer-domain skills and guardrails to production within the Kairos operating environment.
Data scientists and MLOps engineers support propensity, NLP, and decision models across claims, payment integrity, risk adjustment, and care management.
Conversational AI specialists support voice, chat, and virtual-agent deployments across member and provider service operations.
Clinician reviewers and AI-safety reviewers include registered nurses and physicians from the TeleMedik acquisition, bringing a 380+ member URAC-accredited clinical workforce with all-50-state reach to support regulated clinical and utilization workflows under Human-in-the-Loop oversight.
This payer-focused capability is complemented by a broader bench of AI-certified professionals, automation engineers, process-mining specialists, analytics teams, trainers, and healthcare operations experts across the firm. The wider enterprise AI and Digital Services organization supports the payer practice with reusable accelerators, engineering standards, lab infrastructure, and training programs, including AI-powered enablement that has reduced time-to-proficiency and improved quality in operational teams.
Reporting Structure
The capability is governed through Healthcare Solutions leadership in coordination with the broader AI, technology, and governance functions that support Kairos-enabled delivery. Oversight is reinforced through regular leadership reviews, solution-governance checkpoints, and client-facing outcome reviews for strategic engagements.
Top Three Mandates for 2026
Productize and scale Kairos-enabled payer skills and accelerators across claims, service, payment integrity, provider data, and care workflows so that each new engagement starts from reusable domain assets rather than a blank sheet.
Expand payer benchmarks, contextual intelligence, and operational-signal frameworks to strengthen prioritization, traceability, and measurable improvement for clients.
Graduate additional Kairos-enabled workflows to higher autonomy tiers under structured oversight, while extending responsible-AI controls, monitoring, and deployment discipline across the portfolio.
All CoE activity is conducted under our Responsible AI policy framework, aligned to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and EU AI Act Article 10 and 11 requirements, with clinical-safety and regulatory guardrails embedded directly into every Domain Harness skill rather than overlaid as after-the-fact controls.
What is your AI operating model for payor clients — build, buy, partner, or hybrid? Which AI platforms/foundational models do you leverage (e.g., Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex)? (State whether your model is build, buy, partner, or hybrid, and list the specific AI platforms and foundational models used for Healthcare Payor clients with a brief rationale for your approach.)
Hybrid by design. Firstsource builds the layers of the AI stack that compound into proprietary, payer-specific IP; partners on the layers where hyperscaler and platform economics favor scale; and licenses best-in-class specialist solutions where domain-specific platforms are already strong reference points. This is a deliberate architectural choice that protects client value over time, and within this model Kairos serves as the operating environment that ties proprietary skills, contextual intelligence, orchestration, and governance together.
Operating Model — Kairos-led Build, Partner, and License
Built components — the durable, payer-specific IP that compounds with every engagement and is orchestrated through Kairos as the dominant operating system for payer AI:
The Domain Harness part of the Kairos architecture— encoding 25+ years of payer expertise as executable skills, playbooks, and guardrails.
The Intelligent Context Framework (ICF) — capturing canonical member, provider, claim, contract, and clinical entity context, with Decision Traces preserving the full causal chain of every AI-assisted decision.
Operations Intelligence sensors — Process Mining, Object-Centric Process Mining, Task Mining, Conversation Intelligence, Knowledge Mining, and Document Intelligence — surfacing in-flight signal across payer operations.
A growing portfolio of proprietary copilots and agentic workflows, including the Claims and Payment Integrity Copilot, the Claims Agentic AI Workflow, the Customer Service Agentic AI Workflow, the Prior Authorisation Copilot, the Risk Adjustment Copilot, the Care Gap Reviews Copilot, the SARA Instructional Design Copilot, and the WFM Real-Time Adherence Copilot.
Partnered components — the scale layers that plug into Kairos where hyperscaler and platform economics favor broader ecosystem leverage:
Foundational large language models, accessed through hyperscaler enterprise agreements rather than direct model contracts — detailed in the section that follows.
Vector databases, embedding stores, and retrieval infrastructure (Pinecone, OpenSearch, Neo4j).
Hyperscaler infrastructure — Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, and Google Cloud — chosen per engagement to align with the client's preferred cloud.
Licensed components — best-in-class specialist platforms that extend the Kairos operating environment in domains where niche vendors hold the strongest reference capability:
Celonis for Object-Centric Process Mining, Soroco Scout for Task Mining, and HiLabs for healthcare-specific data quality.
Lyzr Agent Studio and Opus Applied AI for agentic workflow orchestration accelerators.
Codoxo and Edifecs for encounter and fraud-waste-abuse submission workflows; Andros for provider credentialing; Simplify Healthcare for network management; Ribbon Health and Perspecta for provider directory data quality.
Foundational Models in Production for Payer Clients
Model selection is made per skill, per client, and per deployment environment rather than as a single firm-wide standard, allowing us to align with each client’s preferred cloud, regulatory posture, and cost-performance requirements. In practice, we leverage enterprise AI ecosystems across Microsoft Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, and Meta/Llama-based ecosystems, alongside specialist AI platforms and open-source tooling where appropriate. Kairos is intentionally model-agnostic: payer skills, context, orchestration, and governance persist independently of whichever foundation model is selected for a given workflow.
Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service — GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, and GPT-4 Turbo — used for the majority of Generative AI workloads under our enterprise Microsoft partnership.
Amazon Web Services Bedrock — Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Claude 3.5 Haiku, and Meta Llama 3 — used for client environments standardised on AWS.
Google Vertex AI — Gemini 1.5 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Flash — used for select engagements, including clients standardised on Google Cloud.
Open-weight models such as Meta Llama 3 and Mistral — fine-tuned and hosted privately for narrowly scoped, high-volume tasks where unit hosting cost is the binding constraint and the workload is well-defined enough to specialise the model.
Specialty Models and AI Capabilities
Beyond foundational language models, we deploy specialty models and frameworks for targeted capabilities such as semantic retrieval, transcription, intent classification, propensity scoring, summarization, document understanding, and workflow orchestration. These are selected according to the use case — for example, payer-document retrieval, contact-center interaction analysis, claims risk scoring, or process-intelligence monitoring — and are composed through Kairos so that domain-specific logic and contextual intelligence remain stable even when underlying models or tools evolve.
Cohere Embed and the OpenAI embedding family for semantic retrieval over payer documents, SOPs, contracts, and clinical guidelines.
OpenAI Whisper for batch transcription; AssemblyAI for real-time transcription in contact-centre and clinical-triage interactions.
XGBoost and DistilBERT for in-house risk-propensity, intent-classification, and Late Payment Interest (LPI) propensity-scoring models.
LangGraph and Temporal for durable agent orchestration; MCP (Model Context Protocol) for structured tool and data integration.
Rationale — Kairos as the durable, model-agnostic operating layer
Kairos is deliberately model-agnostic. Following our first agentic design tenet — separate Brain, Hands, and Memory — the reasoning layer (Brain), the skill library (Hands), and the durable context (Memory) are kept as independent, loosely coupled components. The Domain Harness, part of the Kairos Architecture, the Intelligent Context Framework, and the skill libraries persist as Firstsource and client IP regardless of which foundational model provides reasoning at any given moment. We are able to swap models skill-by-skill, client-by-client, and region-by-region without rewriting our domain assets, which protects clients from vendor lock-in, foundational-model pricing volatility, and the accelerating pace of model deprecation. Equally important, it ensures that 25+ years of payer domain expertise continues to compound inside the durable layers Firstsource owns and operates, rather than inside the foundational models we rent.

How we govern autonomy
Agentic AI introduces operational risk that copilots and traditional automation do not. Firstsource addresses this risk through three reinforcing layers of governance.
Principle-based governance. Every deployment is evaluated against eight standards — fairness, AI for good, regulatory compliance, accountability, interpretability, privacy and security, inclusiveness, and reliability. These principles translate into concrete acceptance criteria during model validation and into ongoing monitoring once a workflow is deployed.
Autonomy calibration through Progressive Trust. We do not deploy agents at full autonomy from day one. Every workflow begins under Human-in-the-Loop review at every decision, where the agent's output is approved or corrected before any downstream action is taken. As we accumulate evidence of sustained accuracy on a defined task, we graduate the workflow to Human-on-the-Loop, where the human supervises the agent's actions rather than approving each one. Only low-risk, high-confidence task domains progress to Human-above-the-Loop autonomy, and continuous post-hoc audit is maintained even at that level. This progression keeps our risk posture conservative and allows us to demonstrate compliance to regulators and clients alike.
Platform-level technical control. Lyzr provides reflection-based validation, groundedness checks against enterprise knowledge sources, fairness and bias safeguards, toxicity monitoring, automated PII detection and redaction, and token-level audit logs. Opus enforces compliance tracking and embeds explicit human review checkpoints at every workflow step.

Responsible AI capabilities
Compliance with CMS and HIPAA for AI-driven decisions
For AI-driven decisions in payor environments, regulatory compliance is enforced at three layers: technical control, process control, and human authority.
At the technical layer, our infrastructure is certified to HIPAA, HITRUST CSF, SOC 2 Type 2, and ISO 27001, with Business Associate Agreements covering every payor client engagement. Encryption, access controls, audit logging, and breach notification capabilities meet or exceed HIPAA Security Rule requirements. For AI-specific governance, our control environment is aligned to ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management systems) and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.
At the process layer, we map each AI deployment to applicable federal and state regulations during use-case design. For prior authorization deployments specifically, our agents are designed to comply with the CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule (CMS-0057-F), including the timeliness mandates that took effect in January 2026. For deployments touching Medicare Advantage coverage decisions, our agents are configured in line with CMS guidance that algorithms and AI models cannot be the sole basis for a coverage or medical necessity determination clinical reviewers retain authority, and AI outputs serve as decision support, not decision-making. Section 1557 non-discrimination requirements are reflected in our fairness testing protocols, and 21st Century Cures Act information-blocking obligations are addressed in our data access patterns.
At the human authority layer, every AI-driven decision that affects a member or provider coverage, payment, authorization, or appeals outcome — is either reviewed by a qualified human or governed by a Progressive Trust autonomy level that has been explicitly authorized by the client. Clinical decisions remain the responsibility of credentialed clinicians; payment decisions remain the responsibility of qualified claims professionals. AI accelerates and informs these decisions; it does not replace the regulated decision-maker.
Firstsource treats Responsible AI not as a policy document, but as an operating model. Every agentic and generative AI deployment in our payor portfolio operates under the same eight-principle Kairos Responsible AI framework, the same Progressive Trust calibration, the same platform-level controls, and the same multi-tier governance ownership. Regulatory compliance with CMS, HIPAA, Section 1557, and state-level requirements are enforced through technical certification, process design, and human authority working together. As regulatory expectations around AI in healthcare continue to evolve, including the CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule and emerging state-level AI accountability legislation, our governance framework is designed to absorb new requirements without disrupting client operations.

What is your AI governance framework for payor clients — including model validation, drift monitoring, audit trails, and rollback mechanisms? (Describe the governance components in place — such as model validation, drift monitoring, audit trails, rollback mechanisms, and governance boards — including the frequency of each activity, who approves models before deployment, how incidents are escalated, and what the rollback SLA is.)
Our AI governance framework for payor clients is designed to make Intelligence that Operates safe, auditable, and production-ready. Kairos acts as the governance operating layer as much as the orchestration layer: it enforces deployment gates, captures traceability, calibrates autonomy through Progressive Trust, and supports rollback when performance or policy conditions require it.
Core governance components
Model validation: design review, data-lineage review, offline validation, fairness and error analysis, and workflow acceptance testing before pilot or production.
Autonomy calibration: workflows begin under Human-in-the-Loop oversight and graduate only after sustained performance and explicit sign-off.
Drift monitoring: production monitoring covers accuracy, confidence, throughput, exceptions, fairness signals, and input-distribution drift.
Audit trails: model version, workflow version, data access, decision path, overrides, and downstream actions are recorded and searchable.
Rollback and incident response: material failures trigger containment, root-cause analysis, rollback to a known-good version or manual fallback, client notification, and documented remediation.
Validation occurs before every material release. Monitoring is typically weekly during stabilization and monthly or quarterly in steady state, depending on risk. Rollback SLAs are defined by use case; for higher-risk workflows, fallback to a prior model or manual mode is typically targeted within hours, not days.
How do you manage data privacy and security when training or fine-tuning AI models on payor member/claims data? (Describe the data privacy controls in place — such as de-identification, synthetic data generation, federated learning, or HIPAA BAAs — including where payor data is stored during training, who has access, how consent and authorization are managed, and any certifications or third-party audits that validate your data privacy posture.)
When training or fine-tuning AI on payor member or claims data, we apply a privacy-by-design model. The starting principle is to use the least sensitive data required, prefer retrieval-grounded or configuration-driven approaches where possible, and where training is required, apply de-identification, access control, contractual controls, and auditable operating procedures throughout the lifecycle. This is managed through Kairos so that data handling, model promotion, and runtime usage remain governed under one operating model.
Core controls
De-identification: Safe Harbor or Expert Determination methods where appropriate; for many GenAI workflows we prefer RAG over broad fine-tuning on raw PHI.
Data minimization: only the minimum fields needed for the task are used; retention is defined by client contract and governance policy.
Logical segregation and access control: client data is segregated by client and environment; access is least-privilege, role-based, logged, and reviewed.
Secure storage and transfer: encryption in transit and at rest, governed environments, and auditable access pathways.
Contractual controls: BAAs, client-approved processing terms, audit rights, and incident-response obligations.
Training and tuning datasets are stored in client-approved cloud or enterprise environments aligned to regulatory and residency requirements. Access is restricted to authorized delivery, engineering, data science, and governance personnel on a documented need-to-know basis, and all access is auditable.

This response is built into Kairos and reinforced through Progressive Trust governance.
Standard response pattern
Detection: alerts, override patterns, QA sampling, fairness checks, client feedback, or exception spikes.
Containment: move to Human-in-the-Loop or manual fallback.
Root-cause analysis: determine whether the issue arose from data drift, policy change, prompt or retrieval error, model degradation, or workflow integration error.
Remediation: recalibration, data refresh, policy update, routing change, model rollback, or additional human review gates.
Disclosure and learning: notify the client per governance terms and feed the lessons back into validation thresholds, monitoring, and deployment standards.

input: Compare Firstsource’s Progressive Trust, auditability, and CMS/HIPAA compliance controls in payor AI governance.
expected_output:
Firstsource’s payor AI governance combines three reinforcing controls:

- **Progressive Trust:** AI autonomy is increased in stages — from **Human-in-the-Loop** to **Human-on-the-Loop** to limited higher autonomy — only after evidence of stable accuracy, quality, fairness, and compliance, plus explicit sign-off. Higher-risk workflows can revert to manual or prior versions within hours if needed.

- **Auditability:** Every AI action is logged with **model/workflow version, data access, decision path, confidence, supporting evidence, human overrides, and downstream actions**. Kairos preserves **Decision Traces** so clients can reconstruct how an output was produced, and records are searchable for compliance reviews and investigations.

- **CMS/HIPAA compliance:** Compliance is enforced through **technical, process, and human authority layers**. Infrastructure is aligned to **HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001**, with BAAs, encryption, role-based access, and logging. CMS requirements are built into workflow design — especially for **prior authorization and coverage decisions**, where AI supports decisions but **qualified clinicians or claims professionals retain final authority** rather than AI acting as sole decision-maker.

In short: **Progressive Trust controls autonomy, auditability ensures traceability, and CMS/HIPAA controls enforce regulatory and privacy compliance in production payor workflows.**

How we govern autonomy
Agentic AI introduces operational risk that copilots and traditional automation do not. Firstsource addresses this risk through three reinforcing layers of governance.
Principle-based governance. Every deployment is evaluated against eight standards — fairness, AI for good, regulatory compliance, accountability, interpretability, privacy and security, inclusiveness, and reliability. These principles translate into concrete acceptance criteria during model validation and into ongoing monitoring once a workflow is deployed.
Autonomy calibration through Progressive Trust. We do not deploy agents at full autonomy from day one. Every workflow begins under Human-in-the-Loop review at every decision, where the agent's output is approved or corrected before any downstream action is taken. As we accumulate evidence of sustained accuracy on a defined task, we graduate the workflow to Human-on-the-Loop, where the human supervises the agent's actions rather than approving each one. Only low-risk, high-confidence task domains progress to Human-above-the-Loop autonomy, and continuous post-hoc audit is maintained even at that level. This progression keeps our risk posture conservative and allows us to demonstrate compliance to regulators and clients alike.
Platform-level technical control. Lyzr provides reflection-based validation, groundedness checks against enterprise knowledge sources, fairness and bias safeguards, toxicity monitoring, automated PII detection and redaction, and token-level audit logs. Opus enforces compliance tracking and embeds explicit human review checkpoints at every workflow step.
Underlying all of this, our infrastructure is certified to ISO 27001, HITRUST, SOC 2 Type 2, and HIPAA. Business Associate Agreements cover every client engagement. Responsible AI capabilities
Compliance with CMS and HIPAA for AI-driven decisions
For AI-driven decisions in payor environments, regulatory compliance is enforced at three layers: technical control, process control, and human authority.
At the technical layer, our infrastructure is certified to HIPAA, HITRUST CSF, SOC 2 Type 2, and ISO 27001, with Business Associate Agreements covering every payor client engagement. Encryption, access controls, audit logging, and breach notification capabilities meet or exceed HIPAA Security Rule requirements. For AI-specific governance, our control environment is aligned to ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management systems) and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.
At the process layer, we map each AI deployment to applicable federal and state regulations during use-case design. For prior authorization deployments specifically, our agents are designed to comply with the CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule (CMS-0057-F), including the timeliness mandates that took effect in January 2026. For deployments touching Medicare Advantage coverage decisions, our agents are configured in line with CMS guidance that algorithms and AI models cannot be the sole basis for a coverage or medical necessity determination clinical reviewers retain authority, and AI outputs serve as decision support, not decision-making. Section 1557 non-discrimination requirements are reflected in our fairness testing protocols, and 21st Century Cures Act information-blocking obligations are addressed in our data access patterns.
At the human authority layer, every AI-driven decision that affects a member or provider coverage, payment, authorization, or appeals outcome — is either reviewed by a qualified human or governed by a Progressive Trust autonomy level that has been explicitly authorized by the client. Clinical decisions remain the responsibility of credentialed clinicians; payment decisions remain the responsibility of qualified claims professionals. AI accelerates and informs these decisions; it does not replace the regulated decision-maker.
Firstsource treats Responsible AI not as a policy document, but as an operating model. Every agentic and generative AI deployment in our payor portfolio operates under the same eight-principle Kairos Responsible AI framework, the same Progressive Trust calibration, the same platform-level controls, and the same multi-tier governance ownership. Regulatory compliance with CMS, HIPAA, Section 1557, and state-level requirements are enforced through technical certification, process design, and human authority working together. As regulatory expectations around AI in healthcare continue to evolve, including the CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule and emerging state-level AI accountability legislation, our governance framework is designed to absorb new requirements without disrupting client operations.

What is your AI governance framework for payor clients — including model validation, drift monitoring, audit trails, and rollback mechanisms? (Describe the governance components in place — such as model validation, drift monitoring, audit trails, rollback mechanisms, and governance boards — including the frequency of each activity, who approves models before deployment, how incidents are escalated, and what the rollback SLA is.)
Our AI governance framework for payor clients is designed to make Intelligence that Operates safe, auditable, and production-ready. Kairos acts as the governance operating layer as much as the orchestration layer: it enforces deployment gates, captures traceability, calibrates autonomy through Progressive Trust, and supports rollback when performance or policy conditions require it.
Core governance components
Model validation: design review, data-lineage review, offline validation, fairness and error analysis, and workflow acceptance testing before pilot or production.
Autonomy calibration: workflows begin under Human-in-the-Loop oversight and graduate only after sustained performance and explicit sign-off.
Drift monitoring: production monitoring covers accuracy, confidence, throughput, exceptions, fairness signals, and input-distribution drift.
Audit trails: model version, workflow version, data access, decision path, overrides, and downstream actions are recorded and searchable.
Rollback and incident response: material failures trigger containment, root-cause analysis, rollback to a known-good version or manual fallback, client notification, and documented remediation.
Validation occurs before every material release. Monitoring is typically weekly during stabilization and monthly or quarterly in steady state, depending on risk. Rollback SLAs are defined by use case; for higher-risk workflows, fallback to a prior model or manual mode is typically targeted within hours, not days.
How do you manage data privacy and security when training or fine-tuning AI models on payor member/claims data? (Describe the data privacy controls in place — such as de-identification, synthetic data generation, federated learning, or HIPAA BAAs — including where payor data is stored during training, who has access, how consent and authorization are managed, and any certifications or third-party audits that validate your data privacy posture.)
When training or fine-tuning AI on payor member or claims data, we apply a privacy-by-design model. The starting principle is to use the least sensitive data required, prefer retrieval-grounded or configuration-driven approaches where possible, and where training is required, apply de-identification, access control, contractual controls, and auditable operating procedures throughout the lifecycle. This is managed through Kairos so that data handling, model promotion, and runtime usage remain governed under one operating model.
Core controls
De-identification: Safe Harbor or Expert Determination methods where appropriate; for many GenAI workflows we prefer RAG over broad fine-tuning on raw PHI.
Data minimization: only the minimum fields needed for the task are used; retention is defined by client contract and governance policy.
Logical segregation and access control: client data is segregated by client and environment; access is least-privilege, role-based, logged, and reviewed.
Secure storage and transfer: encryption in transit and at rest, governed environments, and auditable access pathways.
Contractual controls: BAAs, client-approved processing terms, audit rights, and incident-response obligations.
Training and tuning datasets are stored in client-approved cloud or enterprise environments aligned to regulatory and residency requirements. Access is restricted to authorized delivery, engineering, data science, and governance personnel on a documented need-to-know basis, and all access is auditable.

Standard response pattern
Detection: alerts, override patterns, QA sampling, fairness checks, client feedback, or exception spikes.

Remediation: recalibration, data refresh, policy update, routing change, model rollback, or additional human review gates.
Disclosure and learning: notify the client per governance terms and feed the lessons back into validation thresholds, monitoring, and deployment standards.

Compound agents — running on a combination of LLMs, domain-expert models, and business rules — execute on secure private infrastructure. Knowledge graphs enrich the underlying data so that agents can drive visualization, summarization, care management, clinical record handling, and payment integrity decisions through data chaining, prompting, and APIs. | Administrative cost has reduced, care quality has improved, and member engagement has increased.
6 | AI Workflow Decision Agent (Appeals and Grievances) | PoC | 1 | We designed and piloted an agentic workflow scoped specifically to appeals and grievances. The workflow predicts appeals risk, classifies appeal types, automates case structuring, and drafts compliance-aligned communication. It is integrated with the appeals workflow systems, member and provider data, and policy repositories. | Pilot validation is in progress. We are targeting 99.5%+ urgent-appeals 4-hour TAT compliance and a meaningful reduction in rework volume.
# | Capability | What it does | Tools/frameworks | Implementation in payor environments
1 | Bias detection and fairness | Statistical fairness testing across protected and operational groups (demographics, plan type, line of business, provider segment, geography) at model validation and at production runtime; bias drift monitoring; recalibration workflows when drift exceeds tolerance. | Lyzr fairness and bias safeguards; SHAP/LIME for feature-level disparity analysis; statistical parity, equalized odds, and predictive parity tests; HITRUST AI Assurance Program controls. | For the claims adjudication and prior authorization agents, we test for differential approval rates across member demographics, lines of business, and provider segments before deployment and at scheduled intervals thereafter. Firstsource maintains agreed bias thresholds for every deployment, and where metrics exceed those thresholds, a structured response is initiated: the affected workflow is escalated for human review, the underlying model is recalibrated against the corrected distribution, and where the finding is material to client operations or regulatory obligations, formal disclosure is made to the client with a documented remediation plan.
2 | Explainability and interpretability | Every AI-driven decision is accompanied by a human-readable rationale citing the inputs considered, the logic applied, the supporting policy or guideline, and the confidence level. | SHAP for feature attribution; decision-trail logging; model cards documenting training data, validation results, intended use, and known limitations; natural-language rationale generation for clinical and operational reviewers. | For prior authorization agents, every auto-approval or auto-denial carries a structured explanation citing the relevant payer policy section, clinical guideline, and the specific evidence extracted from the medical record. Reviewers see the same explanation on escalated cases under Human-in-the-Loop, ensuring consistent reasoning across human and AI decisions.
3 | Auditability and traceability | Every agent action, model prediction, data access, and human override is logged with full context — input, decision, confidence, supporting evidence, timestamp, agent or user identity — and retained per client record-retention requirements. | Lyzr token-level audit logs; Opus compliance tracking; immutable append-only audit trails; structured event logs ingested into client and Firstsource SIEM systems; annual third-party audit of the AI control environment. | All AI decisions on payor accounts are retained for the duration required by client record-retention policies (typically seven to ten years for healthcare records). Firstsource makes full audit trails available to clients and regulators on request, searchable by case ID, member ID, provider ID, agent name, and decision type, enabling rapid response to compliance inquiries, internal audits, and regulatory examinations without operational disruption.
4 | Privacy and data protection | Member and claims data flows are protected end-to-end by de-identification where possible, encryption, role-based access, and contractual safeguards. | Automated PII detection and redaction (Lyzr); de-identification under HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination methods; AES-256 encryption at rest; TLS 1.2+ in transit; client-managed or Firstsource HSM-managed encryption keys per client preference. | Training data is de-identified before any model fine-tuning. Production data flows are governed by client-specific Business Associate Agreements. Access follows the minimum necessary standard with audit trails on every access event. Data residency is configurable per client requirements (US-only deployments where mandated).
5 | Human oversight (Progressive Trust) | No agent is deployed at full autonomy from day one. Workflows graduate from Human-in-the-Loop to Human-on-the-Loop to Human-above-the-Loop only after sustained accuracy, bias-test pass, and client sign-off. | Lyzr workflow gates; Opus human checkpoints; Progressive Trust framework documented per deployment; quarterly autonomy reviews. | Every new agentic deployment for a payor client begins under Human-in-the-Loop review on every decision. Graduation requires a minimum 90-day stabilization period, sustained accuracy above the contracted threshold, bias-check pass, and explicit client sign-off documented in the engagement record.

Drift exceeding thresholds triggers root-cause analysis, recalibration, or rollback to a known-good model version within a contracted SLA (typically four hours for material drift).

expected_output:
